definition_zh: 金属丝；电线；（电）电报；铁丝网；汇款
definition_en: a thin thread of metal, especially one carrying electric current, and by extension a telegram or a money transfer
core_image: 一只灰色的盒子背后垂出几根细金属线，指尖一碰有点发麻
scene: 拆开旧收音机，里面盘着几根细金属线，螺丝一松就弹了出来。A loose wire behind the desk was the cause of the short circuit.
sceneCN: 这里 wire 是「电线、金属丝」（第 1 个义项：细细的一根金属线）；句意为桌子后面一根松了的电线导致了短路。盒子里盘着的那几根细线，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 金属丝；电线；电报；铁丝网

collocations.zh: 带电的电线；精力充沛的人

derivatives.zh: 布线；线路
无线的
窃听
有线的；（口语）亢奋的

senses.title: A thin thread of metal
senses.definition: a long thin piece of metal, often bendable, used for holding, shaping or carrying current
senses.definitionCN: 细长可弯的金属条，用来固定、造型或导电
senses.example: The basket was made of thin copper wire.
senses.exampleCN: 这只篮子是用细铜丝编成的。
senses.why: The earliest sense is the drawn metal itself, a thread that could be bent into any shape.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项就是拉制出来的金属本身，一根可以弯成任何形状的线。

senses.title: A conductor of electricity
senses.definition: a metal thread covered with plastic that carries electric current in a building or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 外面包着塑料的金属线，在建筑或机器中输送电流
senses.example: A loose wire behind the desk was the cause of the short circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 桌子后面一根松了的电线导致了短路。
senses.why: Once electric current travelled along drawn metal, the thread of the craftsman became the artery of a house.
senses.whyCN: 电流开始沿着拉制金属走，工匠的那根线就成了房屋的血管。

senses.title: A telegram or a money transfer
senses.definition: a message sent along telegraph wires, or money sent between banks by message rather than in person
senses.definitionCN: 沿电报线发出的讯息，或银行之间以讯息而非现金方式转账的钱
senses.example: The news came by wire from the capital that same evening.
senses.exampleCN: 当晚消息就从首都用电报发了过来。
senses.why: Both messages and money moved along the wire, so the wire itself became the name of the service.
senses.whyCN: 消息和钱都沿着这条线走，于是线本身成了这项业务的名字。

senses.title: To install electric wiring
senses.definition: to fit a building or a device with the wires that carry power or signals
senses.definitionCN: 给建筑或设备装上输电或传信号的线路
senses.example: They wired the old house before moving in.
senses.exampleCN: 搬进去之前他们给老房子装了电线。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, meaning to provide a thing with this new kind of thread.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，意为给某物配上这种新的线。

intro.en: Wire comes from Old English wir, the name of drawn metal worked into jewellery; the electrical sense arrived only in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: wire 来自古英语 wir，是拉制金属、用于制作首饰的名称；与电有关的义项到十九世纪才出现。

items.en: wir named fine drawn metal, used in rings and boxes rather than in machines.
items.cn: wir 指拉制得很细的金属，用于戒指与盒饰，而不是机器。

items.en: The word widened to bowls, strings and instruments, where a thread of metal holds or sings.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到碗、弦与乐器：一根金属线用来系住或发声。

items.en: The telegraph spread the word along its own lines, and a telegram became a wire.
items.cn: 电报让自己的线路把这个词传播开来，一封电报就被称作 wire。

items.en: Electric power gave wire its modern centre: the plastic-coated thread inside every wall.
items.cn: 电力给了 wire 现代的核心义：每一面墙里那根包着塑料的线。

items.en: Banks and later broadcasters produced wire transfers and wireless signals.
items.cn: 银行以及后来的广播人又造出了电汇与无线信号。

note.en: The first group holds look-alikes formed from adjacent letters, the second cables and threads of metal.
note.cn: 第一组收字母相近的形近词，第二组收电缆与金属线。

entries.definition: To clean with one sweep of a cloth.
Broad from one side to the other.
To pay for the use of something.
Thin and strong, like wire.
A thick bundle of wires or fibres.
A thin line of fibre, the picture behind wire.
A very thin strand of material.

normalIntro.en: Wire is short and thin like the thing itself, and its silent e keeps the long i.
normalIntro.cn: wire 像它所指之物一样短而细，末尾的 e 让 i 保持长音。

normal.en: Five letters, all narrow: the word looks like a wire on the page.
normal.cn: 五个字母一个比一个窄，这个词在纸上就像一根线。

normal.en: The silent e keeps the i long, as in fire and hire.
normal.cn: 不发音的 e 保持 i 长音，如 fire、hire。

normal.en: Wiry means thin and strong, so a wiry runner is built like wire.
normal.cn: wiry 意为瘦而结实，所以 a wiry runner 就像金属丝一样的人。

normal.en: Wireless drops the wire: signals travel without it.
normal.cn: wireless 去掉那根 wire：信号不再需要它。

normal.en: A telegram travelled on wires, so in old films a wire is a message.
normal.cn: 电报沿着电线走，所以老电影里 a wire 就是一封电文。

abstract.en: A faint hum heard through the box before it is opened.
abstract.cn: 盒子还没打开，就从里面听见一点嗡声。

abstract.en: A thread of copper catching a single point of light.
abstract.cn: 一根铜丝接住了一个光点。

abstract.en: A jump in the fingertip when the screwdriver touches the wrong spot.
abstract.cn: 螺丝刀碰到不该碰的地方时，指尖一跳。

examples.en: The fence is made of wire and wooden posts.
examples.cn: 这道篱笆由金属丝和木桩做成。

examples.en: Do not touch that wire with wet hands.
examples.cn: 不要用湿手碰那根电线。

examples.en: He wired the money to his brother the same afternoon.
examples.cn: 当天下午他就把钱电汇给了弟弟。

dict_mnemonic.text: fire 换成 w 开头，暖与光变成了细细的「电线、金属丝」。

root: 古英语 wir（拉制的细金属）→ 中古英语 wyr/wire → wire；同族有 wiring、wireless、wiretap。

sensesIntro.en: A drawn thread of metal becomes the carrier of electricity, then a channel for messages and money, and finally a verb of fitting such lines.
sensesIntro.cn: 一根拉制的金属线成为电的载体，再成为消息与金钱的通道，最后变成安装这种线路的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin bright thread of copper bending in the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根弯在手里的细亮铜丝。

branches.en: The metal branch: a basket woven from copper wire.
branches.cn: 金属分支：用铜丝编成的篮子。

branches.en: The current branch: a loose wire behind the desk.
branches.cn: 电流分支：桌后松了的电线。

branches.en: The message branch: news arriving by telegraph.
branches.cn: 消息分支：用电报传来的新闻。

branches.en: The verb branch: an old house fitted with lines.
branches.cn: 动词分支：给老房子装线。

branches.en: The carrier branch: whatever travels quickly takes the line's name.
branches.cn: 载体分支：走得快的东西都借用了线的名字。

intro.en: Wire takes simple endings and forms a rich family: wiring, wireless and the compound barbed wire.
intro.cn: wire 能接简单词尾，构成丰富的一族：wiring、wireless 以及复合词 barbed wire。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Old English; the Latin entry is a borrowed word for a metal thread.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属于古英语；拉丁条目只是借入的表示金属线的词。

items.example: It is the plain noun and verb.

items.meaningCN: 多根电线；第三人称单数

items.meaning: the lines installed in a place
to listen secretly on a line

items.example: The metal thread turned into a barrier.

definition_zh: 撤走；撤回；退出；取（款）；（从活动中）抽身
definition_en: to pull something back or take it out, and to remove oneself from a place, a plan or an activity
core_image: 一只手伸向桌上的文件，忽然停住，又把它抽回到自己身边
scene: 话才说到一半，他伸手想把文件推回去，手指在纸角上停了一下，又慢慢抽了回来。She withdrew her application at the last minute.
sceneCN: 这里 withdraw 是「撤回、收回」（第 1 个义项：把已经拿出或提出的东西抽回来）；句意为她在最后一刻撤回了申请。手指在纸角上停一下又抽回来的那一刻，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 撤回；取款；退出
内向的；不愿交往的
退缩的
前进；推进（反义）

senses.title: To take money out
senses.definition: to take money out of a bank account or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 从银行账户或取款机中取出钱
senses.example: He withdrew two hundred yuan to pay the driver.
senses.exampleCN: 他取了二百元付给司机。
senses.why: The verb pulls something from where it was kept, and money in an account is simply a thing kept somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把东西从它被存放的地方拉出来，账户里的钱也只是存放在某处的东西。

senses.title: To take back a statement or offer
senses.definition: to say that something you offered or said is no longer in force
senses.definitionCN: 声明自己提出或说过的事不再有效
senses.example: She withdrew her application at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一刻撤回了申请。
senses.why: Once a word or a paper has been handed over, pulling it back means putting it out of play.
senses.whyCN: 一旦话或文件交了出去，把它拉回来就意味着作废。

senses.title: To leave a place or activity
senses.definition: to remove troops or oneself from a place, a contest or an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 把军队或自己从某地、某场比赛或某组织中撤出
senses.example: The team withdrew from the competition after two injuries.
senses.exampleCN: 两人受伤之后，这支队伍退出了比赛。
senses.why: The physical picture of pulling back became a public act of leaving a stage.
senses.whyCN: 往回拉的身体画面，成了退出舞台的公开行为。

senses.title: To pull away into oneself
senses.definition: to become quiet and avoid other people, often because of worry or hurt
senses.definitionCN: 变得沉默、回避他人，常因忧虑或受伤
senses.example: After the quarrel he withdrew into his own room for days.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵之后他躲进自己的房间里好些天。
senses.why: The same motion turned inward describes a person drawing back from company.
senses.whyCN: 同样的动作转向内心，就形容一个人从人群中退回去。

intro.en: Withdraw is a native compound: the old prefix with-, meaning away or back, joined to draw, to pull.
intro.cn: withdraw 是本土复合词：古前缀 with-（离开、往回）加上 draw（拉）。

items.en: wið meant against or away, and dragan meant to draw or pull, so the pair named pulling back.
items.cn: wið 意为对着或离开，dragan 意为拉，两者合起来就是往回拉。

items.en: Early uses described drawing back a hand, an arrow or a knife.
items.cn: 早期用法描述把手、箭或刀抽回来。

items.en: The compound widened to pulling troops back from a place.
items.cn: 复合词扩展到把军队从某地撤回。

items.en: Banking gave the everyday sense of taking money out of an account.
items.cn: 银行业给了它从账户取钱这一日常义项。

items.en: Modern use adds leaving a competition and drawing away from people emotionally.
items.cn: 现代用法又加上了退出比赛与情感上疏远他人。

note.en: The first group collects members of the with- family and look-alikes, the second verbs of taking back or leaving.
note.cn: 第一组收 with- 家族成员与形近词，第二组收表示收回或离开的动词。

entries.definition: The noun of taking back or out.
To refuse to give something due.
To resist and bear pressure.
The past form of the verb.
To move back from an enemy or a difficulty.
Formally to take back a statement.
To put money into an account.

normalIntro.en: Withdraw splits neatly into with and draw, so the picture is simply drawing something back.
normalIntro.cn: withdraw 干净地分成 with 与 draw 两半，画面就是往回拉东西。

normal.en: With plus draw: draw back what you once put out.
normal.cn: with 加 draw：把曾经伸出去的东西拉回来。

normal.en: The past tense is withdrew, with the same vowel change as drew.
normal.cn: 过去式 withdrew，元音变化与 drew 一致。

normal.en: The past participle withdrawn ends like known and shown.
normal.cn: 过去分词 withdrawn 的结尾像 known、shown。

normal.en: Take out money or take back a promise: both are pulling, one from a box and one from a mouth.
normal.cn: 取钱与收回承诺都是拉：一个从箱子里，一个从嘴里。

normal.en: Withhold only holds, so it refuses; withdraw pulls, so it removes.
normal.cn: withhold 只是握住，所以是拒绝给；withdraw 是拉，所以是拿掉。

abstract.en: A hand hesitating over the corner of a paper.
abstract.cn: 一只手在纸角上方犹豫。

abstract.en: A crowd thinning at the edge of the field.
abstract.cn: 场地边缘渐渐稀疏的人群。

abstract.en: A door closing quietly from the inside.
abstract.cn: 一扇从里面轻轻关上的门。

examples.en: The bank charges a fee to withdraw cash abroad.
examples.cn: 在国外取现银行会收手续费。

examples.en: They withdrew the product after a safety warning.
examples.cn: 一则安全警告之后，他们撤下这款产品。

examples.en: Several countries withdrew from the talks.
examples.cn: 有几个国家退出了谈判。

dict_mnemonic.text: with（往回）+ draw（拉）—— 往回拉，就是「撤回、取款」。

root: 古英语 wið（离开、对着）+ dragan（拉）→ withdraw；同族有 withdrawal、withhold、withstand。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as pulling a thing back, then takes money from an account, a promise from circulation, and a person from a stage or from company.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从往回拉开始，接着从账户取钱、让承诺作废，再把人从舞台或人群中撤回。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pulling a document back towards the chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把文件拉回胸前。

branches.en: The money branch: cash taken out for a taxi.
branches.cn: 金钱分支：取出现金付车钱。

branches.en: The promise branch: an application pulled back.
branches.cn: 承诺分支：被撤回的申请。

branches.en: The public branch: a team leaving a competition.
branches.cn: 公共分支：退出比赛的队伍。

branches.en: The private branch: days spent alone in a room.
branches.cn: 私人分支：独自待在房里的几天。

branches.en: The inward branch: the same pull, now aimed at oneself.
branches.cn: 内向分支：同一个拉的动作，如今朝向自己。

intro.en: Withdraw takes the old prefix with- and the root draw, then adds -al to make the noun withdrawal.
intro.cn: withdraw 由古前缀 with- 与词根 draw 组成，再加 -al 得到名词 withdrawal。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic; the Latin entries below are borrowed cousins for the idea of pulling back.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都属于日耳曼语；下面的拉丁条目只是表示「拉回」的借入表亲。

definition_zh: 经受住；抵挡；抵抗；承受住压力、攻击或诱惑
definition_en: to be strong enough not to be damaged, defeated or changed by something
core_image: 狂风撞向岩石，岩石一动不动，风只好绕着走
scene: 台风过境，玻璃窗被吹得嗡嗡作响，却始终没碎。The bridge was built to withstand winds of up to two hundred kilometres an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 withstand 是「经受住、抵挡」（第 1 个义项：强壮到不被破坏或击败）；句意为这座桥按能抵挡每小时两百公里的风速来建造。

pos.zh: 动词：经受住、抵挡、抵抗；承受得住

derivatives.zh: 不规则过去式与过去分词，义为「经受住了」
现在分词，义为「正在抵挡」
第三人称单数形式，义为「（他/它）抵挡得住」
加 -er 构成，较少用，义为「抵御者」

senses.title: To bear a force
senses.titleCN: 经受住：承受住外力而不被破坏
senses.definition: to be strong enough to bear a force without being damaged
senses.definitionCN: 强壮到能承受外力而不受损坏
senses.example: The roof is designed to withstand heavy snow.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶的设计能承受大雪。
senses.why: The word joins with, here meaning against, and stand: to stand against a force is to remain standing under it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 with（此处意为「对着」）与 stand「站立」组成：对着外力仍然站住，就是承受住它。

senses.title: To resist attack
senses.definition: to resist an attack or pressure, especially military or verbal
senses.definitionCN: 抵御攻击或压力，尤指军事或言辞上的
senses.example: The walls withstood the siege for three months.
senses.exampleCN: 城墙在围攻下坚持了三个月。
senses.why: The standing image turns defensive: the one who stands does not fall and does not yield.
senses.whyCN: 「站」的意象转为防御性的：站住的人既不倒，也不退。

senses.title: To survive a test of time
senses.titleCN: 经受住考验：历时长久而不坏
senses.definition: to remain in good condition or in force over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期保持良好状态或仍然有效
senses.example: Few ideas withstand the test of time.
senses.exampleCN: 能经受住时间考验的想法并不多。
senses.why: Time is treated as a force like wind or water: the metaphor of physical resistance is extended to endurance.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当成风与水那样的外力：物理抵抗的比喻延伸为持久。

senses.title: To resist temptation
senses.titleCN: 抵挡诱惑：不被人心所动
senses.definition: to refuse to give in to a desire or an influence
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝向欲望或影响屈服
senses.example: He withstood the temptation to open the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他抵住了拆开那封信的诱惑。
senses.why: Here nothing physical presses: what must be stood against is one's own wish, and the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 此处并无实体在压迫：需要顶住的是自己的意愿，而同一个动词兼管两者。

senses.title: To endure hardship
senses.definition: to get through a difficult period without being broken by it
senses.definitionCN: 度过艰难时期而未被击垮
senses.example: The family withstood months of cold and hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 这一家人熬过了数月的寒冷与饥饿。
senses.why: The older sense of standing firm shades into endurance: not just not falling, but keeping on.
senses.whyCN: 「站稳」的旧义滑向「忍受」：不只是不倒，还要继续撑下去。

intro.en: Withstand is an Old English compound of with, here meaning against, and stand: to stand against something.
intro.cn: withstand 是古英语复合词，由 with（此处意为「对着、反对」）与 stand「站」构成：对着某物站住。

items.en: Widstandan meant 'to stand against, to oppose, to resist', with wid- carrying the hostile sense of against.
items.cn: 古英语 widstandan 意为「对着站、反对、抵抗」，其中 wid- 带「对着、敌对」之义。

items.en: The prefix with- once meant against in many verbs, as in withhold and withdraw.
items.cn: 前缀 with- 曾在一大批动词中表示「对抗」，如 withhold、withdraw。

items.en: The verb belongs to an old group of compounds whose first element meant against or away.
items.cn: 这个词属于一组古老的复合词，其第一个成分意为「对着」或「离开」。

items.en: Withstonden kept both the physical sense of bearing a force and the moral sense of resisting.
items.cn: 中古英语 withstonden 同时保留「承受外力」的物理义与「抗拒」的道德义。

items.en: The past form withstood was fixed by analogy with stood, and the verb spread to tests of weather, time and desire.
items.cn: 过去式 withstood 依 stood 类推而定形，动词后来扩展到天气、时间与欲望的考验。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other with- compounds and the stand family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of resisting and enduring.
note.cn: 形近组收其他 with- 复合词与 stand 一族；近义组收表示抵抗与忍耐的动词。

entries.definition: To hold something back; another with- compound.
entries.definitionCN: 同前缀复合词，义为「扣住、不给」。

entries.definition: To draw back or take out; the prefix again means away.
entries.definitionCN: 同前缀复合词，义为「撤退、取出」。

entries.definition: To grasp a meaning; formed with stand but unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 形近词，义为「理解」，也由 stand 构成但来源不同。

entries.definition: The irregular past tense and past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 派生形式，即不规则过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: To push back against something, from Latin; broader and more neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抵抗」，源自拉丁语，范围更广、更中性。

entries.definition: To bear pain or hardship over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受」，强调长时间承受痛苦与艰苦。

entries.definition: To carry or put up with something; the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承受」，最平实的日常用词。

entries.definition: To come through something and still exist.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「幸存」，强调事后仍然存在。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English compound with-stand and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语复合词 with-stand，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Withstand is with in its old sense of against plus stand: to stand against.
normal.cn: withstand 就是取 with 的旧义「对着」加 stand：对着站住。

normal.en: The prefix with- also means against in withhold and withdraw.
normal.cn: 前缀 with- 在 withhold、withdraw 中也表示「对抗」。

normal.en: Withstand the test of time is the most common abstract use.
normal.cn: withstand the test of time 是最常见的抽象用法。

normal.en: The past tense is withstood, built on stood.
normal.cn: 过去式是 withstood，由 stood 类推而来。

normal.en: Buildings and bridges are described as built to withstand storms.
normal.cn: 建筑与桥梁常说 built to withstand storms。

abstract.en: Picture a rock facing a gale: the wind must go around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块迎风的岩石：风只能绕过去。

abstract.en: The word measures strength by what remains after the force has passed.
abstract.cn: 这个词用外力过后剩下什么来衡量强度。

abstract.en: Standing is the whole idea: whatever does not fall has withstood.
abstract.cn: 「站着」就是全部：没有倒下的，就是经受住了。

examples.en: The tower has withstood earthquakes for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座塔经受住了六百年来的地震。

examples.en: These plants can withstand long periods without rain.
examples.cn: 这些植物能耐受长时间无雨。

examples.en: She withstood pressure from every side and kept her decision.
examples.cn: 她顶住了各方的压力，坚持了自己的决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为着站」——为着站住不倒，就得抵住风暴：经受住

root: 古英语 wid「对着、反对」+ standan「站」→ widstandan → 英语 withstand；同族有 withstood、withhold、withdraw。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of withstand all rest on standing against something: a physical force, an attack, the wear of time, a temptation, and a stretch of hardship.
sensesIntro.cn: withstand 的五个义项都建立在「对着站住」上：物理外力、攻击、时间磨损、诱惑，以及一段艰苦。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rock in a gale, unmoved while the wind bends around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：狂风中的岩石，纹丝不动，风只能绕行。

branches.en: THE FORCE: roofs and bridges built to carry snow and wind.
branches.cn: 外力线：为承受雪与风而建的屋顶、桥梁。

branches.en: THE ATTACK: walls that hold against a siege.
branches.cn: 攻击线：围城之下仍不倒的城墙。

branches.en: THE TIME: ideas that withstand the test of time.
branches.cn: 时间线：经受住时间考验的想法。

branches.en: THE DESIRE: the temptation not opened.
branches.cn: 欲望线：抵住而没有拆开的诱惑。

branches.en: THE HARDSHIP: a family that gets through cold and hunger.
branches.cn: 艰苦线：熬过寒冷与饥饿的一家人。

intro.en: Withstand is a native compound: the old prefix with- meaning against plus the strong verb stand.
intro.cn: withstand 是本族复合词：旧前缀 with-（意为「对抗」）加强动词 stand。

latinIntro.en: With- and stand are both Germanic; the Latin words for resisting, resistere and sustinere, are unrelated in form.
latinIntro.cn: with- 与 stand 都属日耳曼语；拉丁语表示抵抗的 resistere、sustinere 在形态上与之无关。

items.example: It carries the hostile sense in withstand and withhold.
items.exampleCN: 它在 withstand、withhold 中带对抗义。

items.example: It is the base verb of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个复合词的本动词。

items.example: It forms the past tense withstood.
It builds resist, the Latin-side near synonym.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 resist，即拉丁系的近义词。

items.example: It builds sustain, a Latin cousin in meaning.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 sustain，是语义上的拉丁表亲。

definition_zh: 目击者；证人；证词；目击；见证（某事件）
definition_en: a person who sees an event happen, and to see or to give evidence about an event
core_image: 街角的一个路人停下脚步，眼睛一直没离开那扇正在被推开的门
scene: 事故发生时，街角有个路人停下脚步，一直盯着那扇被撞开的门。The only witness to the accident was a boy of twelve.
sceneCN: 这里 witness 是「目击者」（第 1 个义项：亲眼看见某事发生的人）；句意为事故唯一的目击者是一个十二岁的男孩。街角那个停下脚步、眼睛不离开的人，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 目击证人
证人席
有见证的
证词

senses.title: A person who saw it
senses.definition: a person who was present and saw an event with their own eyes
senses.definitionCN: 在场并亲眼看见某事件的个人
senses.example: The only witness to the accident was a boy of twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 事故唯一的目击者是一个十二岁的男孩。
senses.why: The old noun came from a word meaning knowledge, so a witness was first simply someone who knew.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老名词来自意为「知识」的词，所以 witness 起初只是知道的人。

senses.title: A person in a court
senses.definition: someone who tells a court under oath what they saw or know
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上宣誓讲述所见所知的人
senses.example: She appeared as a witness for the family.
senses.exampleCN: 她作为这家人的证人出庭。
senses.why: The same knowledge is now official: the witness speaks to a judge and the words become evidence.
senses.whyCN: 同样的知识成了正式的：证人向法官陈说，其话成为证据。

senses.title: To see an event happen
senses.definition: used of a person, place or time that sees an event take place
senses.definitionCN: 用于人、地点或时代看见某事件发生
senses.example: That year witnessed the biggest flood in a century.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年发生了一世纪以来最大的洪水。
senses.why: Places and years can be said to witness, so the word widens from people to the settings of events.
senses.whyCN: 地点与年份也能「见证」，于是这个词从人扩展到事件的发生场景。

senses.title: To show that something is true
senses.definition: to provide evidence of a fact, in phrases such as bear witness to
senses.definitionCN: 在 bear witness to 等说法中，为某事实提供证明
senses.example: The empty shelves bore witness to the long drought.
senses.exampleCN: 空空的货架说明旱情已久。
senses.why: If a person can tell what happened, then an object can also stand as a silent proof of it.
senses.whyCN: 如果人能讲述发生了什么，物件也能成为它的无声证明。

intro.en: Witness comes from Old English witnes, formed from witan, to know, so the witness was the one who knows what happened.
intro.cn: witness 来自古英语 witnes，由 witan（知道）构成，所以证人就是知道发生了什么的人。

items.en: witnes meant knowledge as well as a person who has it, built on witan, to know.
items.cn: witnes 既指知识，也指拥有知识的人，建于 witan（知道）之上。

items.en: The word moved towards the legal sense, a person who reports what he saw.
items.cn: 这个词转向法律义，指报告自己所见的人。

items.en: To bear witness and to call a witness fixed the noun in legal speech.
items.cn: bear witness 与 call a witness 让名词在法律语言里固定下来。

items.en: The verb came to be used of places and periods that see great events.
items.cn: 动词开始用于看见大事的地点与时期。

items.en: Silent objects, from a broken wall to an empty shelf, can now bear witness as well.
items.cn: 无声的物件，从断墙到空货架，如今也能作证。

note.en: The first group gathers same-family and look-alike words, the second other names for someone who reports events.
note.cn: 第一组收同族与形近词，第二组收其他指讲述事件者的称呼。

entries.definition: The plural or third person form.
The place where a witness stands in court.
A woman who serves food at tables.
A wild and empty natural area.
A person who watches carefully.
A person who is there but does not take part.
Facts that show what is true.

normalIntro.en: Witness is wit plus -ness, so the spelling keeps a single t in the middle and a single n after it.
normalIntro.cn: witness 是 wit 加 -ness，所以中间只有一个 t，后面只有一个 n。

normal.en: Wit plus ness: the one who has wit and knows what happened.
normal.cn: wit 加 ness：有见识、知道发生了什么的那个人。

normal.en: Do not double the t: it is wit, not witt, before ness.
normal.cn: t 不要写两个：加 ness 前是 wit 而非 witt。

normal.en: The plural takes -es after the s sound of ness.
normal.cn: 复数在 ness 后的 s 音后加 -es。

normal.en: An eye witness is a witness with eyes, which is all a witness ever is.
normal.cn: eye witness 意为带眼睛的证人，而证人本来就是眼睛。

normal.en: Bear witness means carry the proof, as one bears a heavy thing to court.
normal.cn: bear witness 意为把证据扛到法庭，如扛起重物。

abstract.en: Feet stopping at a corner and not moving.
abstract.cn: 在街角停住、不再移动的脚步。

abstract.en: Eyes fixed on a door as it opens.
abstract.cn: 门被推开时那双不移的眼睛。

abstract.en: A hand raised in a silent room, ready to speak.
abstract.cn: 安静的房间里举起、准备开口的手。

examples.en: Two witnesses described the same car.
examples.cn: 两名目击者描述的是同一辆车。

examples.en: We are witnessing the end of an old habit.
examples.cn: 我们正在见证一种旧习惯的终结。

examples.en: The marks on the wall bear witness to the flood.
examples.cn: 墙上的痕迹证明了那次洪水。

dict_mnemonic.text: wit（知道）+ ness —— 知道真相的那个人，就是「证人」。

root: 古英语 witan（知道）→ witnes（知识；知情者）→ witness；同族有 eyewitness、wit。

sensesIntro.en: The one who knows becomes the one who speaks in court, then the verb spreads to places and years, and finally to silent objects.
sensesIntro.cn: 知道的人成为在法庭上讲述的人，接着动词扩展到地点与年份，最后扩到无声的物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a passer-by stopped dead at a corner, watching.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角一个停住脚步的路人在看。

chain: A PLACE OR YEAR THAT SEES

branches.en: The observer branch: a boy of twelve at the corner.
branches.cn: 观察者分支：街角上十二岁的男孩。

branches.en: The court branch: a family's supporter on the stand.
branches.cn: 法庭分支：证人席上支持那家人的她。

branches.en: The event branch: a year that saw a great flood.
branches.cn: 事件分支：见到大洪水的那一年。

branches.en: The proof branch: marks on a wall that tell the story.
branches.cn: 证据分支：墙上讲述往事的痕迹。

branches.en: The evidence branch: seeing and proving are the same act.
branches.cn: 证据分支：看见与证明是同一个行为。

intro.en: Witness is the stem wit with the noun ending -ness; the same history gives the adjective witnessly in old texts.
intro.cn: witness 是词干 wit 加名词词尾 -ness；同样来历在古文中还留下 witnessly 这样的形式。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin entry shows the borrowed legal word for a witness, still used in testis-based terms.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属于日耳曼语；拉丁条目给出法律上的借入词，仍留在以 testis 为词根的说法里。

items.example: The root of the whole family.
The noun turned into an action.

items.exampleCN: 身份给了一处地方命名。

definition_zh: 想知道；纳闷；感到惊讶；惊奇；奇迹；奇观
definition_en: to want to know something, or to feel surprise and admiration; also the feeling or the thing that causes it
core_image: 夜里抬头看见满天星，脖子一直往后仰，忘了低头
scene: 孩子第一次被带到郊外，抬头看星星看了很久，一句话也不说。I wonder whether the old shop is still open after all these years.
sceneCN: 这里 wonder 是「想知道」（第 1 个义项：心里存着疑问，很想知道答案）；句意为我想知道这么多年过去那家老店是否还开着。夜里仰头看满天星，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 奇迹；奇观；令人惊叹的事物

derivatives.zh: 由 wonder 加 -ful 构成，义为「极好的；精彩的」
由 wonder 加 -ing 构成，义为「好奇的；疑惑的」
由 wonder 加 -ous 构成，义为「奇妙的；令人惊叹的」
由 wonder 加 -ment 构成，义为「惊奇；惊讶之情」

senses.title: To want to know
senses.definition: to feel a wish to know something, often said softly before a polite question
senses.definitionCN: 心里很想弄明白某事，常用在礼貌的提问之前
senses.example: I wonder whether the old shop is still open after all these years.
senses.exampleCN: 我想知道这么多年过去那家老店是否还开着。
senses.why: The old root means to gaze in astonishment, and a mind that keeps gazing turns into a mind that keeps asking.
senses.whyCN: 古老的词根意思是惊讶地凝视，一直望下去的心就变成了不断发问的心。

senses.title: To be struck by something
senses.definition: to feel surprise mixed with admiration when something is greater than expected
senses.definitionCN: 遇到超出预期的事物时，感到惊讶又钦佩
senses.example: The children wondered at the size of the whale in the museum hall.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们望着大厅里那头鲸的骨架，惊讶得说不出话。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the body stops and stares because the sight is too large to take in.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：身体停下凝视，因为眼前的景象大得接不住。

senses.title: The feeling itself
senses.definition: the feeling of surprise and admiration that such a sight leaves behind
senses.definitionCN: 那样的景象留下的那份惊讶与钦佩
senses.example: She looked at the night sky with wonder, forgetting the cold.
senses.exampleCN: 她满怀惊奇地望着夜空，忘了冷。
senses.why: Once the staring ends, what remains inside is the feeling, so the name turns into a noun.
senses.whyCN: 凝视结束之后，留在心里的是那种感受，于是这个名字变成了名词。

senses.title: The thing that causes it
senses.definition: a person or thing so extraordinary that it makes people stare and admire
senses.definitionCN: 极其非凡、让人驻足赞叹的人或物
senses.example: The bridge was counted among the wonders of the ancient world.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥被列为古代世界的奇观之一。
senses.why: By a natural shift, the cause of the staring takes the same name as the staring itself.
senses.whyCN: 很自然的一次转移，让引起凝视的东西和凝视本身用了同一个名字。

intro.en: Wonder comes from Old English wundor, a noun for a marvel, related to words for astonishment in the other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: wonder 来自古英语名词 wundor（奇事），与其他日耳曼语中表示惊讶的词同源。

items.en: wundor named a marvel or a portent, something that stopped people in their tracks.
items.cn: wundor 指奇事或征兆，是让人停下脚步的东西。

items.en: Cousin words in the old Germanic languages also mean a marvel, which points to one shared root.
items.cn: 各门古老日耳曼语里的同源词也表示奇事，指向一个共同词根。

items.en: The noun softened to wonder and gained the sense of a feeling as well as a thing.
items.cn: 名词演变为 wonder，既指事物，也开始指一种感受。

items.en: The verb to wonder developed, first meaning to marvel at, then to be curious.
items.cn: 动词兴起来，先表示对某事惊叹，后来表示好奇。

items.en: The polite opener of requests, as in wonder if, became fixed in everyday speech.
items.cn: 作为礼貌开场的 wonder if，在日常口语中固定下来。

note.en: The first group holds the same stem in other shapes, the second holds other words for curiosity and surprise.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干的其他形态，第二组收其他表示好奇与惊讶的词。

entries.definition: Extremely good or enjoyable.
Feeling curious or puzzled.
Marvellous, amazing, a little literary.
To be filled with wonder, or a wonderful thing.
A strong wish to know or learn something.
A feeling of respect mixed with wonder and fear.

normalIntro.en: Wonder is one stem used as verb and noun: the same word means to stare, to ask, and the thing worth staring at.
normalIntro.cn: wonder 是同一个词干兼作动词和名词：既指凝视，也指发问，还指值得凝视的东西。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling, so context alone tells you which is meant.
normal.cn: 名词和动词拼写相同，只能靠上下文判断。

normal.en: No wonder is a frozen phrase that still carries the old idea of marvel.
normal.cn: no wonder 是固定说法，仍带着「奇事」的旧意。

normal.en: Add -ful and the marvel becomes an adjective of praise: wonderful.
normal.cn: 加 -ful，奇事就变成赞美的形容词 wonderful。

normal.en: Wonder if is the soft way to ask a question, not a claim of not knowing.
normal.cn: wonder if 是婉转发问的方式，不是在声称不知道。

normal.en: Wonder and wander differ by one letter: one stays still and stares, the other walks away.
normal.cn: wonder 与 wander 只差一个字母：一个驻足凝视，一个走开。

abstract.en: A neck tipped back so far that the sky fills the whole face.
abstract.cn: 脖子仰得太久，整张脸都是天空。

abstract.en: A question that has no sharp edges yet.
abstract.cn: 一个还没有长出尖角的问题。

abstract.en: A hand lifted but not yet touching the stone of the old bridge.
abstract.cn: 手举起来了，却还没碰到老桥的石头。

examples.en: I wonder why she left without saying goodbye.
examples.cn: 我想知道她为什么不告而别。

examples.en: The children stared at the sea in wonder.
examples.cn: 孩子们惊奇地望着大海。

examples.en: It is no wonder that he passed the exam after months of study.
examples.cn: 他苦读了几个月，通过考试一点也不奇怪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「望的」——一直往前望着的那个东西，就是让人惊奇的「奇迹」。

root: 古英语名词 wundor（奇事、奇迹），与日耳曼语同源词共同指向「惊奇地凝视」这一核心意象；后派生动词义。

sensesIntro.en: From a stopped body the meaning spreads: first to be struck, then to be curious, then to the feeling, and finally to the thing worth staring at.
sensesIntro.cn: 意义从一个停住的身体散开：先是感到震撼，再是好奇，接着是那份感受，最后是值得凝视的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a neck tipped back until the sky fills the face.
core.cn: 核心意象：仰头到整张脸都是天空。

branches.en: The asking branch: a soft question about the old shop.
branches.cn: 发问分支：轻声问起那家老店。

branches.en: The staring branch: children lost before a whale skeleton.
branches.cn: 凝视分支：孩子在鲸骨架前出神。

branches.en: The feeling branch: wonder under the night sky.
branches.cn: 感受分支：夜空下的惊奇。

branches.en: The marvel branch: a bridge counted among ancient wonders.
branches.cn: 奇观分支：跻身古代奇迹的桥。

branches.en: The everyday branch: no wonder marks surprise that has become ordinary.
branches.cn: 日常分支：no wonder 标记已经平常的惊讶。

intro.en: Wonder is a plain Germanic stem; the endings it takes, such as -ful and -ous, only colour the marvel into adjectives.
intro.cn: wonder 是朴素的日耳曼语词干；它加上的 -ful、-ous 等词尾，只把这件奇事染成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is native Germanic, so there is no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below are cousins of the same idea only.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词只是同一想法的表亲。

items.meaning: a marvel, or to stare and ask
items.example: The stem carries both noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干兼作名词与动词。

items.example: The old marvel sense survives here.
items.exampleCN: 古老的奇事义在此保留。

items.example: The participle shows the stopped body.
items.exampleCN: 分词部分呈现停住的身体。

definition_zh: 极好的；精彩的；美妙的；令人惊叹的
definition_en: extremely good, pleasant, or impressive, so that it makes you stop and admire
core_image: 端上一盘刚出锅的菜，全桌人同时「哇」了一声
scene: 第一次尝到朋友做的家乡菜，桌上几个人都放下筷子先看着它。The view from the top of the pass was wonderful in the early morning light.
sceneCN: 这里 wonderful 是「极好的、美妙的」（第 1 个义项：好到让人惊叹）；句意为清晨光线下从山口望下去的景致美得惊人。一桌人同时「哇」出声，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wonderful 加 -ly 构成，义为「极好地；奇妙地」
由 wonderful 加 -ness 构成，义为「美妙；极好」
去掉 -ful 得到的名词，义为「惊奇；奇迹」

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: so good or pleasant that it draws praise without effort
senses.definitionCN: 好得或愉快得让人自然而然地称赞
senses.example: We had a wonderful time at the small restaurant by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河边那家小馆子度过了非常愉快的时光。
senses.why: The suffix -ful says full of, so the marvel of wonder is poured into a whole adjective of praise.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ful 表示「充满」，于是 wonder 的惊奇被灌进一个纯粹赞美的形容词。

senses.title: Marvellous to look at
senses.definition: so striking or beautiful that people stop to admire it
senses.definitionCN: 非常醒目的、美的，让人停下来欣赏
senses.example: The view from the top of the pass was wonderful in the early morning light.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨光线下，从山口望下去的景致美得惊人。
senses.why: The older layer of wonder means a marvel, and the landscape here still keeps that sense of staring.
senses.whyCN: wonder 更古老的一层意思是奇事，这里的风景仍保留着那种凝视的感觉。

senses.title: Remarkably skilled or kind
senses.definition: used of a person or a quality that is better than one expects
senses.definitionCN: 用于人或某种品质，好得超出预期
senses.example: Her wonderful patience made the long wait almost pleasant.
senses.exampleCN: 她那了不起的耐心让漫长的等待几乎变得愉快。
senses.why: Praise moves from things to people, so the same adjective describes a quality that impresses.
senses.whyCN: 称赞从物转到人，同一个形容词便用来描述令人佩服的品质。

intro.en: Wonderful is the native noun wonder, a marvel, with the suffix -ful added to say full of marvels.
intro.cn: wonderful 由本土名词 wonder（奇事）加后缀 -ful 构成，意为「充满奇事的」。

items.en: The noun wundor named a marvel, and the suffix -ful meant full of.
items.cn: 名词 wundor 指奇事，后缀 -ful 表示充满。

items.en: The two parts joined as wonderful in the sense of full of wonders.
items.cn: 两部分组合成 wonderful，意思满是奇事。

items.en: Everyday speech stretched it into a general word of praise.
items.cn: 日常口语把它引申为泛用的赞美词。

items.en: The gradable use with more and most settled, since the suffix blocks -er.
items.cn: 因为后缀不能用 -er，比较级与最高级固定用 more 和 most。

items.en: In current use the adjective is milder than the noun, closer to very good than to miraculous.
items.cn: 如今这个形容词比名词温和，更接近「很好」而不是「奇迹般」。

note.en: The first group holds words cut from the same stem, the second holds other adjectives of strong praise.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干切出的词，第二组收其他表示强烈赞美的形容词。

entries.definition: A marvel, or the feeling of amazement.
In an excellent or marvellous way.
Marvellous, chiefly literary.
Extremely good or surprising, British spelling.
Extremely good, informal and enthusiastic.
Impressive and fine, a little formal.

normalIntro.en: Wonderful is wonder plus the ending -ful, so the word literally says full of marvels.
normalIntro.cn: wonderful 就是 wonder 加 -ful，字面上就是「满是奇事」。

normal.en: Keep the double l of -ful: only the adverb wonderfully adds one more l before -y.
normal.cn: 记住 -ful 里的双 l：只有副词 wonderfully 会在 -y 前再多一个 l。

normal.en: The ending -ful means full of, so wonderful is full of wonder.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ful 表示充满，所以 wonderful 就是满是惊奇。

normal.en: Because of the suffix, the comparison takes more and most, never -er.
normal.cn: 由于这个后缀，比较级用 more 和 most，从不用 -er。

normal.en: Wonderfully adds -ly and keeps both l letters, giving three in a row.
normal.cn: wonderfully 加 -ly 时保留两个 l，于是连出三个 l。

normal.en: Wonder is the noun and wonderful the adjective, a pair like help and helpful.
normal.cn: wonder 是名词，wonderful 是形容词，正像 help 与 helpful 这一对。

abstract.en: A whole table going quiet at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 整桌人在同一瞬间安静下来。

abstract.en: Light on water that makes the eye refuse to blink.
abstract.cn: 水上的光让眼睛不愿意眨。

abstract.en: A word that has grown lighter than its root.
abstract.cn: 一个比它的词根更轻的词。

examples.en: Thank you for a wonderful evening.
examples.cn: 谢谢你给了我这么一个愉快的夜晚。

examples.en: It was a wonderful surprise to see her at the station.
examples.cn: 在车站见到她真是个美妙的惊喜。

examples.en: The old gardener told wonderful stories about the trees.
examples.cn: 老园丁讲了很多关于这些树的奇妙故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「万得福」——万事都得到福气，日子当然「极好」。

root: 古英语 wundor（奇事）+ 本土后缀 -ful（充满）→ wonderful；词根意象是「惊奇地凝视」。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from things that are simply very good, to sights that stop people, and finally to people who impress.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从单纯很好的事物，走到让人停步的景象，最后走到令人佩服的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole table going quiet at the first taste.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一口之后整桌人安静下来。

branches.en: The praise branch: a wonderful evening at a small restaurant.
branches.cn: 赞美分支：小馆子里的愉快夜晚。

branches.en: The sight branch: a pass lit by early sun.
branches.cn: 景象分支：晨光里的山口。

branches.en: The person branch: patience that impresses everyone.
branches.cn: 人分支：让人佩服的耐心。

branches.en: The mild branch: current use is gentler than the noun.
branches.cn: 温和分支：今用比名词温和。

branches.en: The gradable branch: more wonderful, most wonderful.
branches.cn: 程度分支：more wonderful、most wonderful。

intro.en: Wonderful is a native stem plus the old suffix -ful, and it is that suffix which shapes the comparison.
intro.cn: wonderful 是本土词干加古老后缀 -ful，正是这个后缀决定了它的比较级写法。

latinIntro.en: Neither part is Latin; the words below are borrowed cousins of the same idea of marvel.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不是拉丁语；下面的词只是借来的、同表「奇迹」这一想法的表亲。

items.exampleCN: 它由 wonder 构成 wonderful。

items.example: It is replaced by more wonderful.
The same stem forms this noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干可构成这个名词。
它构成文学色彩的 wondrous。

definition_zh: 木材；木头；树林；林地；木（球杆；乐器类别）
definition_en: the hard material of trees used for building, or a small forest; also the hard core of a golf club
core_image: 刚锯开的木头横截面，年轮一圈套一圈，还带着潮气
scene: 院子里新锯断的树桩还没搬走，切面上能数出一圈圈的年轮。The table is made of old oak wood that has turned dark with time.
sceneCN: 这里 wood 是「木材、木头」（第 1 个义项：树木的坚硬材料，用来做东西）；句意为这张桌子是用年久变深的老橡木做的。新锯开的横截面上能数出年轮，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wood 加 -en 构成，义为「木制的；僵硬的」
由 wood 加 -y 构成，义为「木质化的；树木茂密的」
由 wood 与 land 复合，义为「林地」
由 wood 与 work 复合，义为「木工活；木制部件」

senses.title: The material of a tree
senses.definition: the hard substance inside a tree, cut and used for building or burning
senses.definitionCN: 树干内部的坚硬物质，砍下后用于建造或燃烧
senses.example: The table is made of old oak wood that has turned dark with time.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子是用年久变深的老橡木做的。
senses.why: The oldest meaning is the substance itself, the part of the tree that can be carried away and used.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是那种物质本身，也就是树身上能够搬走使用的那部分。

senses.title: A small forest
senses.definition: a piece of land covered with growing trees, smaller than a forest, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 一片长着活树的土地，比 forest 小，常用复数
senses.example: We walked through the woods behind the farm until it got dark.
senses.exampleCN: 我们穿过农舍后面的树林，一直走到天黑。
senses.why: Where the material grows in plenty, the same name serves for the place, and the plural marks the many trees.
senses.whyCN: 那种材料长得多的地方也用了同一个名字，复数则点出许多棵树。

senses.title: The hard core of a club
senses.definition: the solid block of a golf club that strikes the ball, once made of wood
senses.definitionCN: 高尔夫球杆击球的那块实心部分，早年用木头制成
senses.example: He hit the ball with the wood instead of the iron on the short hole.
senses.exampleCN: 那洞很短，他用木杆而不是铁杆击球。
senses.why: Because clubs were once carved from hard timber, the material name stuck to the part.
senses.whyCN: 因为球杆早年用硬木削成，材料名就留在了那个部件上。

senses.title: A wooden sound
senses.definition: used to describe a wooden or dull quality, or the section of an orchestra that was once wooden
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容木质的、发闷的特质，也指乐团中过去用木制成的声部
senses.example: The wood section began softly, and the strings came in a beat later.
senses.exampleCN: 木管声部轻轻开始，弦乐晚了一拍进来。
senses.why: Material used as an adjective easily becomes a label for sound or class, not only for substance.
senses.whyCN: 材料名作形容词用，很容易变成声音或类别的标签，而不只是指物质。

intro.en: Wood is Old English wudu, meaning both the tree and its timber, and the same stem survives in the Dutch and German names for wood.
intro.cn: wood 来自古英语 wudu，既指树也指木材，同一词干还见于荷兰语和德语的「木头」。

items.en: wudu named both a growing tree and the timber cut from it.
items.cn: wudu 既指生长着的树，也指砍下的木材。

items.en: Cousin words in Dutch and German still mean wood or forest.
items.cn: 荷兰语与德语的同源词仍表示木头或森林。

items.en: The final vowel weakened, and the form settled toward wode and later wood.
items.cn: 词尾元音弱化，形式向 wode 过渡，最终成为 wood。

items.en: The wooden adjective took the old ending -en, as in golden and silken.
items.cn: 木制的形容词采用了古老的词尾 -en，就像 golden 与 silken。

items.en: The plural woods narrowed mostly to the place sense, the trees standing together.
items.cn: 复数 woods 主要收窄到地方义，即聚在一起的树。

note.en: The first group holds words grown from the same stem, the second holds other words for timber and for small forests.
note.cn: 第一组收同根长出的词，第二组收其他泛指木材与树林的词。

entries.definition: Made of wood; also stiff and unnatural.
Having a lot of wood in it, or full of trees.
Land covered with trees.
Wood prepared for building, often large beams.
Timber cut into rough boards, chiefly American.
A large area thickly covered with trees.

normalIntro.en: Wood is one short native word with a double life: growing trees and the timber cut from them.
normalIntro.cn: wood 是一个简短的本土词，过着双重生活：既指活树，也指砍下来的木头。

normal.en: The plural woods usually means a place full of trees, not several materials.
normal.cn: 复数 woods 通常指满是树的地方，而不是好几种木头。

normal.en: Wooden takes the old ending -en, the same one in golden.
normal.cn: wooden 用古老的词尾 -en，与 golden 相同。

normal.en: Woody adds -y and keeps both letters of the stem: wood plus y.
normal.cn: woody 加 -y 时保留词干的两个字母：wood 加 y。

normal.en: Do not confuse wood with would: one is material, the other a helping verb.
normal.cn: 别把 wood 与 would 混了：一个是材料，一个是助动词。

normal.en: Woodland and woodwork are compounds that join a second common word.
normal.cn: woodland 与 woodwork 都是复合词，后面接一个常用词。

abstract.en: Rings counted on a fresh stump.
abstract.cn: 在新鲜的树桩上数年轮。

abstract.en: A grain that pulls a nail slightly to one side.
abstract.cn: 木纹让钉子微微歪向一边。

abstract.en: Warmth that comes from a wall of old beams.
abstract.cn: 一面旧梁柱墙传来的温度。

examples.en: The old chair is carved from a single block of wood.
examples.cn: 这把旧椅子是用一整块木头雕成的。

examples.en: They gathered dry wood for the fire before nightfall.
examples.cn: 天黑前他们捡好了烧火用的干柴。

examples.en: A path runs through the woods behind the village school.
examples.cn: 一条小路穿过村小学后面的林子。

root: 古英语 wudu（树；木材），与荷兰语、德语同源；加 -en 得 wooden，加 -y 得 woody。

sensesIntro.en: The material comes first, then the place where it grows, then the part of an object once cut from it, and finally the dull wooden quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是材料，再是长材料的地方，接着是用它削成的部件，最后是发闷的木质质感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rings counted on a freshly cut stump.
core.cn: 核心意象：在刚锯开的树桩上数年轮。

branches.en: The material branch: a table of old oak wood.
branches.cn: 材料分支：老橡木做的桌子。

branches.en: The place branch: a walk through the woods at dusk.
branches.cn: 地方分支：黄昏穿过林子。

branches.en: The club branch: a wooden head striking the ball.
branches.cn: 球杆分支：木制杆头击球。

branches.en: The sound branch: the wood section of an orchestra.
branches.cn: 声音分支：乐团的木管声部。

branches.en: The quality branch: wood as a word for stiffness and dullness.
branches.cn: 质感分支：wood 用来形容僵硬与发闷。

intro.en: Wood is a bare native stem; the endings -en and -y are what turn the material into adjectives.
intro.cn: wood 是一个不带词缀的本土词干；把材料变成形容词的是 -en 与 -y 两个词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic with no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below name the same material from another branch.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词从另一支语系来指同一种材料。

items.meaning: tree material or a small forest

items.exampleCN: 它使 wood 成为 woods。

items.meaning: a task or a made thing
a picture printed from a wood block

definition_zh: 羊毛；毛线；毛料；毛纺织品
definition_en: the soft thick hair of sheep and some other animals, or the yarn and cloth made from it
core_image: 一大团刚从羊身上剪下的毛，捏一把会慢慢弹回来
scene: 冬天到了，奶奶翻出那团一直没用完的毛线，开始给孙辈织围巾。This sweater is pure wool, so it stays warm even when it gets wet.
sceneCN: 这里 wool 是「羊毛、毛线」（第 1 个义项：羊身上柔软浓密的毛，也指用它纺成的线）；句意是这件毛衣是纯羊毛的，湿了也仍然暖和。捏一把会慢慢弹回来的毛团，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wool 加 -en 构成，义为「羊毛制的」
由 wool 加 -y 构成，义为「毛茸茸的；模糊的」
由 woolen 转作名词，义为「毛织品；毛料衣服」

senses.title: The fleece of the sheep
senses.definition: the soft thick hair that grows on sheep and some other animals, cut off once a year
senses.definitionCN: 羊及少数其他动物身上柔软浓密的毛，每年剪一次
senses.example: The farmer sells the wool from his sheep every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫每年春天卖掉羊身上的羊毛。
senses.why: This is the living source: the coat of the animal before anyone spins it.
senses.whyCN: 这是活的源头：还没被人纺过的动物皮毛。

senses.title: The spun thread
senses.definition: the yarn made by twisting the fibre, sold in balls for knitting
senses.definitionCN: 把纤维捻成的纱线，常以团为单位出售供编织
senses.example: Grandmother wound the wool into a ball before she started the scarf.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶先把毛线绕成团，才动手织围巾。
senses.why: Once the fibre is twisted, the same word follows it into the ball on the table.
senses.whyCN: 纤维一旦被捻成线，这个词就跟着它走进桌上那团线里。

senses.title: The woven cloth
senses.definition: the cloth woven from the yarn, used for coats and suits
senses.definitionCN: 用这种线织成的布料，用于外套和西装
senses.example: This sweater is pure wool, so it stays warm even when it gets wet.
senses.exampleCN: 这件毛衣是纯羊毛的，湿了也仍然暖和。
senses.why: From the ball to the loom is one more step, and the material name covers the finished cloth too.
senses.whyCN: 从线团到织机只差一步，材料名便也涵盖了织成的布。

senses.title: Being pulled back
senses.definition: used in the fixed phrase "pull the wool over someone's eyes", meaning to trick them
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定说法「pull the wool over someone's eyes」，意即欺骗某人
senses.example: He tried to pull the wool over her eyes, but she had checked the figures.
senses.exampleCN: 他想蒙骗她，但她早已核过数字。
senses.why: The soft fibre of a wig or a hood once hid the eyes, so the material stands for a blindfold.
senses.whyCN: 早年假发或兜帽的柔软毛料会遮住眼睛，于是这种材料成了蒙眼布的代称。

intro.en: Wool is Old English wull, shared with German Wolle and Dutch wol, and going back to a reconstructed root for the fleece.
intro.cn: wool 来自古英语 wull，与德语 Wolle、荷兰语 wol 同源，可上溯到一个表示羊毛的重构词根。

items.en: wull named the fleece of the sheep and the cloth made from it.
items.cn: wull 指羊的毛以及用它制成的布。

items.en: The same word for fleece appears across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 相同的「羊毛」一词出现在各门日耳曼语中。

items.en: The vowel shortened and the spelling settled on wool.
items.cn: 元音变短，拼写固定为 wool。

items.en: The endings -en and -y built woollen and woolly.
items.cn: 词尾 -en 与 -y 造出 woollen 与 woolly。

items.en: Idioms such as "pull the wool over someone's eyes" fixed the word in everyday speech.
items.cn: 「pull the wool over someone's eyes」之类的成语让这个词进入日常口语。

note.en: The first group holds the forms built on the same stem, the second holds other textile words that often meet it.
note.cn: 第一组收同根构成的词形，第二组收常与它相遇的其他纺织词。

entries.definition: Made of wool, British spelling.
Made of wool, the American spelling.
Soft and fuzzy, or unclear in outline.
The coat of wool on a sheep.
Thread spun from fibre for knitting.
The soft white fibre of the cotton plant.

normalIntro.en: Wool is a short native word with a doubled vowel spelling but a single short sound.
normalIntro.cn: wool 是一个简短的本土词，两个 o 只读一个短音。

normal.en: Two o letters, one short vowel sound: wool rhymes with full.
normal.cn: 两个 o 只读一个短元音：wool 与 full 押韵。

normal.en: Woollen and woolen are two spellings of the same adjective, British and American.
normal.cn: woollen 与 woolen 是同一个形容词的英式与美式拼写。

normal.en: Woolly doubles the l before -y; the other spelling keeps -en instead.
normal.cn: woolly 在 -y 前双写 l；另一种拼写则用 -en。

normal.en: Cotton wool is not wool at all, which shows how the word can mean soft fibre in general.
normal.cn: cotton wool 根本不是羊毛，可见这个词也可泛指柔软的纤维。

normal.en: The idiom "pull the wool over his eyes" comes from a soft cloth hiding the eyes.
normal.cn: 成语「pull the wool over his eyes」源自用软布遮眼。

abstract.en: A handful of fleece that slowly springs back into shape.
abstract.cn: 一把羊毛慢慢弹回原样。

abstract.en: The smell of a sweater dried near a fire.
abstract.cn: 在火边烘干的毛衣的气味。

abstract.en: A year of warmth carried in two hands.
abstract.cn: 一整年的温暖捧在两只手里。

examples.en: This coat is lined with thick wool for the winter.
examples.cn: 这件外套用厚羊毛做衬，适合冬天。

examples.en: She bought three balls of wool to knit a scarf.
examples.cn: 她买了三团毛线来织围巾。

examples.en: Nobody could pull the wool over his eyes after that mistake.
examples.cn: 出了那次错以后，谁也别想蒙他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捂」——冬天用羊毛把脖子捂得严严的。

root: 古英语 wull（羊毛），与德语 Wolle、荷兰语 wol 同源；-en 与 -y 分别构成 woollen、woolly。

sensesIntro.en: The fleece comes first, then the thread twisted from it, then the cloth woven from the thread, and finally the soft blindfold of an idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是羊毛，再是捻成的线，接着是织成的布，最后是那句成语里的软蒙眼布。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handful of fleece springing back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把会弹回来的羊毛。

branches.en: The source branch: wool sold from the farm each spring.
branches.cn: 源头分支：农场每年春天卖羊毛。

branches.en: The yarn branch: a ball of wool before knitting.
branches.cn: 纱线分支：织之前的线团。

branches.en: The cloth branch: a coat that stays warm when wet.
branches.cn: 布料分支：湿了也暖的外套。

branches.en: The trick branch: the soft cloth over the eyes.
branches.cn: 欺骗分支：遮在眼前的软布。

branches.en: The material branch: one word from the sheep to the coat.
branches.cn: 材料分支：一个词从羊到外套。

intro.en: Wool is a bare stem; -en and -y are the endings that turn it into adjectives.
intro.cn: wool 是裸词干；-en 与 -y 是把它变成形容词的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below name wool or fleece from another branch.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词从另一支来指羊毛。

items.example: It names the same coat before shearing.

definition_zh: 劳动力；全体员工；在岗人员总数
definition_en: all the people who work in an organization, industry or country, considered as a body
core_image: 厂门口的招工启事与车间里三班倒的人，人事部在册页上清点人数
scene: 厂区门口贴着招工启事，车间三班倒，人事部正在清点在册人数。 The plant's workforce has grown by a third since the new line opened.
sceneCN: 这里 workforce 指「某单位的全部在岗人员」（第 1 个义项：一个组织或地区里工作的全体人员）；句意为新生产线投产以来，这家工厂的员工总数增加了三分之一。图中可辨识物件：招工启事、打卡机、排班表、在册名单、安全帽。

senses.title: All the people who work in one organization
senses.titleCN: 一个组织里的全体工作人员
senses.definition: the whole body of people employed by a single firm, plant or institution
senses.definitionCN: 一家公司、工厂或机构雇用的全部人员
senses.example: The plant's workforce has grown by a third since the new line opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新生产线投产以来，这家工厂的员工总数增加了三分之一。
senses.why: Work and force join to mean 'the strength available for work', and an organization's strength is simply the people on its books.
senses.whyCN: work 与 force 组合指「可供工作的力量」，而一个组织的力量就是它名册上的人。

senses.title: The total labour supply of a place
senses.titleCN: 一个地区的劳动力总量
senses.definition: the number of people in a country or region who are available for work
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区里可供使用的工作人数
senses.example: Half the national workforce is now employed in services.
senses.exampleCN: 全国劳动力目前有一半受雇于服务业。
senses.why: Economics needs a single figure for the labour a place can put to use, and the compound supplies exactly that countable body.
senses.whyCN: 经济学需要一个数字表示一个地方能投入的劳动，这个复合词恰好提供了这样一个可清点的整体。

senses.title: The staff a manager can deploy
senses.titleCN: 管理者可调配的员工队伍
senses.definition: the body of employees treated as a resource to be assigned and moved
senses.definitionCN: 被当作可分配、可调动的资源来看待的全体员工
senses.example: The new director reorganized the workforce into three regional teams.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管把员工队伍重组为三个区域团队。
senses.why: The second element of the compound is the same word for physical force, so people are spoken of as a strength to be directed.
senses.whyCN: 复合词的第二部分与「力量」同词，因此人被说成一股可被调遣的力量。

senses.title: The people assigned to one task
senses.definition: the particular group of workers given over to a project or operation
senses.definitionCN: 专门投入某个项目或作业的那一群工作者
senses.example: A workforce of two hundred was assembled for the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 为这条隧道集中了两百人的施工队伍。
senses.why: Because the compound names a body rather than an individual, it can be counted for a single undertaking.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词指一个整体而非个人，因此可以按单项工程来计人数。

senses.title: The employed part of the population
senses.definition: those who currently hold paid work, as contrasted with the unemployed
senses.definitionCN: 当前有报酬工作的人，与失业者相对
senses.example: The survey separated the workforce from those who had stopped looking.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把在业人口与已停止求职的人分开统计。
senses.why: Statistical use needs a line between people with jobs and people without, and this compound marks the side with jobs.
senses.whyCN: 统计上需要在有工作与没工作的人之间划一条线，这个复合词标记的是有工作的一侧。

senses.title: The collective skills of the staff
senses.titleCN: 员工技术与能力的总和
senses.definition: the sum of what the employees can do, treated as an asset of the firm
senses.definitionCN: 员工能力的总和，被视为公司的一项资产
senses.example: The merger was valued mainly for its experienced workforce.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并的价值主要在于对方有经验的员工队伍。
senses.why: Once 'force' is read as capacity, the compound can mean capacity in the sense of skill rather than head count.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 force 读作「能力」，这个复合词便可指技能意义上的能力，而不只是人头数。

senses.title: Organized labour in an industry
senses.titleCN: 行业层面的劳动者群体
senses.definition: the workers of a trade or sector viewed as one interest
senses.definitionCN: 把某个行业或部门的工人视为一个整体利益
senses.example: The union speaks for a workforce of nine thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工会代表九千名工人。
senses.why: Collective bargaining requires a single counterpart, so the compound also names workers as an organized body.
senses.whyCN: 集体谈判需要一个单一对手方，因此这个复合词也把工人称作一个有组织的整体。

senses.title: The pool of people who could be drawn into work
senses.titleCN: 可被吸纳进工作的潜在人力
senses.definition: the wider reserve, including those not yet working, from which employers may recruit
senses.definitionCN: 包括尚未工作的人在内的更大储备，雇主可从中招人
senses.example: Childcare costs keep many trained people out of the workforce.
senses.exampleCN: 托育费用使许多受过训练的人无法进入劳动力队伍。
senses.why: When the word is used of what is 'in' or 'out of' it, the reference shifts from those working to all who might work.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词被说成「在」或「不在」其中时，所指便从正在工作的人转向所有可能工作的人。

intro.en: Workforce is a modern English compound, joining the native noun work with force, which came into English from Old French and ultimately from Latin fortis 'strong'. It belongs to the language of management and national accounts. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: workforce 是近代英语复合词，由英语本族名词 work 加 force 构成；force 经古法语进入英语，最终出自拉丁 fortis「强壮」。它属于管理与国民核算的语言。年代均为约数。

items.en: Weorc meant 'work, deed, something made', from a Germanic root shared by German Werk and Dutch werk; it is native, not borrowed.
items.cn: weorc 意为「工作、行为、做成之物」，出自与德语 Werk、荷兰语 werk 同源的日耳曼词根，是英语本族成分，不是借词。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong'; its noun fortia gave Old French force 'strength, power, violence', which English borrowed.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮」；其名词 fortia 演成古法语 force「力量、权力、强力」，英语借入后者。

items.en: The two words were joined in the twentieth century to name the labour available to an employer or a country, a term that belongs to personnel management and national accounting.
items.cn: 两个词在 20 世纪合起来指雇主或国家可用的劳动，这一术语属于人事管理与国民核算。

items.en: Earlier 'force of work' could mean the strength a task demands; the modern sense keeps only the people, and the strength they represent moves into the background.
items.cn: 早期「工作的力量」可指任务所需的气力；现代义只保留人，人所代表的力量退到背景里。

items.en: Labour statistics adopted the compound for the count of people in work, and from there it entered ordinary news language.
items.cn: 劳动统计采用这个复合词来计在业人数，此后它进入日常新闻语言。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first printed use of the closed compound is not firmly dated, and whether it arose in American personnel writing or in British labour statistics is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个连写复合词最早印行于何时没有可靠年代，它起于美国人事实务写作还是英国劳动统计，亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds compounds and near forms built on the same two words; the second holds terms for the same people counted a different way.
note.cn: 第一组是用同样两个词构成的复合词与形近形式；第二组是用另一种口径统计同一群人的术语。

entries.definition: The spaced spelling of the same term; modern style guides prefer the closed form for the collective sense.
entries.definitionCN: 同一术语的分写形式；现代体例指南在集合义上更倾向连写。

entries.definition: The building or setting where work happens; it shares the first element but names a location.
entries.definitionCN: 工作发生的场所；共享第一个成分，但指地点。

entries.definition: The amount of work assigned to a person or team; it measures the task, not the staff.
entries.definitionCN: 分配给个人或团队的工作量；衡量任务，不衡量人员。

entries.definition: A desk or machine set up for one worker; it names equipment rather than the body of staff.
entries.definitionCN: 为一名工作者配置的工位或机器；指设备而非员工整体。

entries.definition: The employees of a particular organization taken as a group; it rarely extends to a whole country.
entries.definitionCN: 某一组织的员工整体；很少扩展到整个国家。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same statistical idea, often including the unemployed who are seeking work.
entries.definitionCN: 同一统计概念的英式拼法，常包含正在求职的失业者。

entries.definition: The people employed by an organization, viewed through hiring and records; it sounds official.
entries.definitionCN: 从招聘与档案角度看的一个组织的受雇者；语气正式。

entries.definition: An older term for the number of people available for work, framed as physical capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的术语，指可用人数，框定为体能式的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real relatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合结构、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Work plus force: the strength a place can put to work is the people on its books.
normal.cn: work 加 force：一个地方能投入工作的力量，就是它名册上的人。

normal.en: The family runs work, worker, workplace, workload, workforce.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 work、worker、workplace、workload、workforce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases place the word: skilled workforce, aging workforce, enter the workforce.
normal.cn: 固定说法给出位置：技术型劳动力、老龄化劳动力、进入职场。

normal.en: Force here is the Latin fortis 'strong', so the second half is about strength, not coercion.
normal.cn: 这里的 force 是拉丁 fortis「强壮」，因此后半讲的是力量，不是强制。

normal.en: The word is a body, so it takes a singular verb: the workforce has grown.
normal.cn: 这个词指一个整体，因此动词用单数：员工总数已经增长。

abstract.en: Picture a reservoir behind a dam, measured in people rather than litres.
abstract.cn: 想象坝后的一座水库，只是它的计量单位是人而不是升。

abstract.en: Picture a shift board where every name is a slot that can be filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一块排班板，每个名字都是可以被填上的格子。

abstract.en: Picture a firm's balance sheet listing skills where money usually goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张公司资产负债表，在通常写钱的那一栏写着技能。

examples.en: The factory retrained its workforce rather than closing the plant.
examples.cn: 这家工厂选择再培训员工，而不是关厂。

examples.en: An aging workforce changes what products a town can sell.
examples.cn: 劳动力老龄化会改变一座城镇能卖什么产品。

examples.en: Automation cut the workforce by half in five years.
examples.cn: 自动化在五年内把员工人数削减了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「work（工作）+ force（力量）」——一个单位能投入工作的那股力量 → 全体员工、劳动力

root: 英语本族 work（古英语 weorc「工作」）+ force（古法语 force，出自拉丁 fortis「强壮」）。20 世纪合成，指雇主或国家可用的劳动；force 在此取「力量」义而非「强制」义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the people on one firm's books and widen step by step: a country's supply, a manager's resource, a project's crew, the employed half of a population, its skills, an organized body and finally the reserve outside the door.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一家公司名册上的人开始，逐级放宽：一个国家的供给、管理者手中的资源、某项目的队伍、人口中的在业部分、这些人的技能、一个有组织的群体，最后是门外那支储备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate with a hiring notice on it, and a roster inside counting the people who pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门，门上贴着招工信，门内一本名册在清点进出的人。

branches.en: FROM ONE FIRM TO ONE COUNTRY: the same body is counted at the scale of an employer and at the scale of a nation.
branches.cn: 由一家到一国：同一个整体既可按雇主规模计，也可按国家规模计。

branches.en: RESOURCE AND CREW: once people are a strength, they can be assigned to a department or to a single job.
branches.cn: 资源与队伍：人一旦成为一股力量，便可被分派到某个部门或某项工程。

branches.en: COUNT AND CAPACITY: statistics count heads, while valuation counts what those heads can do.
branches.cn: 人数与能力：统计数人头，估值则数这些人会做什么。

branches.en: ORGANIZED BODY: bargaining turns the crowd into a single counterpart.
branches.cn: 有组织的整体：谈判把人群变成一个单一对手方。

branches.en: THE RESERVE OUTSIDE: the word also reaches people not yet working, who could still be drawn in.
branches.cn: 门外的储备：这个词也伸向尚未工作、但仍可被吸纳的人。

intro.en: The compound joins a native English noun to a Latin-derived noun, so its two halves belong to different layers of the vocabulary and bring different relatives.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把英语本族名词与拉丁来源名词接在一起，两半分属词汇的不同层次，也带来不同的同族词。

latinIntro.en: Old English weorc gives work, worker, workshop and workload; Latin fortis gives force, forte, effort and reinforce.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 weorc 衍生 work、worker、workshop 与 workload；拉丁 fortis 衍生 force、forte、effort 与 reinforce。

items.structure: work (native English noun, from Old English weorc)
items.meaningCN: 为达成某事而做的活动
items.example: The first half names the activity itself.
items.exampleCN: 前半部分命名活动本身。

items.structure: force (English noun, from Old French, from Latin fortia)
items.example: The second half names strength rather than compulsion.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分指力量，而非强迫。

items.example: Each worker signs the roster at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 每名工人在门口的名册上签到。
这个工作场所有两个班次。

items.example: The workload doubled after the merger.
The plan is workable within a year.
Her forceful argument carried the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 她有力的论证使会议倒向她一边。

items.example: Extra staff reinforced the night crew.
