definition_zh: 车间；作坊；研讨会；工作坊
definition_en: a room or building where things are made or repaired, or a short class where people work together on a subject
core_image: 一张长桌，工具挂在墙上排成一行，木屑落进沟槽里
scene: 学校的旧仓库被清出来，一半摆了台锯，一半摆了椅子。The workshop on writing lasted all Saturday morning and everyone left with a draft.
sceneCN: 这里 workshop 是「车间、工作坊」（第 1 个义项：制作或修理东西的房间）；句意为那个写作工作坊办了一整个周六上午，每个人走时都带着初稿。工具挂成一排的长桌，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 研讨会；工作坊（短期集体研习）

derivatives.zh: 第一成分，义为「工作」
第二成分，义为「店铺；工场」
由 workshop 加 -er 构成，义为「工作坊参与者」

senses.title: The room where things are made
senses.definition: a room or building with tools where goods are made or repaired
senses.definitionCN: 备有工具、用来制作或修理物品的房间或建筑
senses.example: The carpenter keeps his tools in a small workshop behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 木匠把工具放在屋后一个小作坊里。
senses.why: Shop once meant a place where work is done, so the compound simply says the place of working.
senses.whyCN: shop 原指干活的地方，因此这个复合词直接就是「干活之处」。

senses.title: A place of repair
senses.definition: a garage or small business that repairs machines or vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 修理机器或车辆的车库或小店
senses.example: The bus went back to the workshop with a broken door.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆公交因车门坏了开回了修理车间。
senses.why: Repair is making in reverse, so a garage keeps the name of the place where things are made.
senses.whyCN: 修理是倒过来的制作，于是修车的车库也沿用了「制作之处」这个名字。

senses.title: The shared study
senses.definition: a short session where a small group learns by doing and discussing together
senses.definitionCN: 小群体边做边讨论来学习的短期课程
senses.example: The workshop on writing lasted all Saturday morning and everyone left with a draft.
senses.exampleCN: 那个写作工作坊办了一整个周六上午，每个人走时都带着初稿。
senses.why: The meaning moved from the room where things are made to the meeting where ideas are made together.
senses.whyCN: 意义从「制作东西的房间」挪到了「一起做出想法的聚会」。

senses.title: The room of ideas
senses.definition: a meeting of specialists who work on one problem or draft
senses.definitionCN: 专家聚在一起处理某一问题或稿件的会议
senses.example: A workshop of six teachers produced the new course plan in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 六位老师组成的研习会两天就做出了新课程方案。
senses.why: When experts join hands on one problem, the meeting itself is a workshop where the plan is made.
senses.whyCN: 当专家为一件事携手时，这场会本身就是一个把方案做出来的车间。

intro.en: Workshop joins work with shop, a word that first meant a place where work is done, not a place that sells.
intro.cn: workshop 是 work 与 shop 的复合，shop 最初指干活的地方，而不是卖东西的地方。

items.en: weorc meant labour, and the word for a working place grew from it.
items.cn: weorc 指劳作，表示劳动场所的词由此而生。

items.en: A workshop was the room where a craft was carried out.
items.cn: workshop 指进行手艺活的房间。

items.en: With factories the word widened to any building of machines and benches.
items.cn: 随着工厂出现，这个词扩展到任何有机器和长台的建筑。

items.en: Teachers borrowed it for a short course where students work, not listen.
items.cn: 教师借用它，指学生动手而非只听讲的短期课程。

items.en: The sense of meeting to produce something together is now very common.
items.cn: 聚在一起共同做出成果的这个义项如今非常常见。

note.en: The first group holds compounds sharing the second element, the second holds other places and events of work.
note.cn: 第一组收与它共用后一部分的复合词，第二组收其他工作场所与活动。

entries.definition: A place of trade, or a place of work.
Labour, or a job.
The working area inside a workshop.
A room where an artist or maker works.
A class or meeting for discussion of a subject.
A building where goods are made in large numbers.

normalIntro.en: Workshop is two very common words joined, and the second one has shifted from place of work to meeting.
normalIntro.cn: workshop 是两个极常见词的复合，后半部分从「干活的地方」挪到了「聚会」。

normal.en: Shop here is not a store; the old sense is a place where work is done.
normal.cn: 这里的 shop 不是商店，旧义是干活的地方。

normal.en: Keep both halves when writing: workshop, with no hyphen in current use.
normal.cn: 两半都要写全：workshop，现今不加连字符。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: workshops.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：workshops。

normal.en: A writing workshop works with drafts, not with wood, which shows the figure at work.
normal.cn: 写作工作坊用的是草稿而不是木头，可见这个比喻怎么运作。

normal.en: Attend or run a workshop: the verb pair follows the event sense.
normal.cn: attend a workshop 或 run a workshop，动词搭配跟着活动义走。

abstract.en: Sawdust settled in the groove of a long bench.
abstract.cn: 木屑落进长台的沟槽里。

abstract.en: Chairs pulled into a circle around a half-finished plan.
abstract.cn: 椅子围成一圈，中间是半成品方案。

abstract.en: Two rooms that share one idea of making.
abstract.cn: 两个房间共享一个「做」的想法。

examples.en: The car has been in the workshop for three days.
examples.cn: 这辆车在修理厂放了三天。

examples.en: The teacher runs a small workshop on speaking in public.
examples.cn: 这位老师主持一个小型的公开演讲工作坊。

examples.en: Dust covered every surface of the workshop by the end of the week.
examples.cn: 到周末，车间每处表面都是灰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝可学」——车间里窝着就能学到手艺。

root: work（劳作）+ shop（旧义「干活的地方」）→ workshop；后引申为「工作坊、研讨会」。

sensesIntro.en: The room of craft comes first, then the room of repair, then the meeting where ideas are made in the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是手艺的房间，再是修理的房间，接着是用同样方式做出来自想法的聚会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tools hanging in a row above a long bench.
core.cn: 核心意象：长台上面挂成一排的工具。

branches.en: The craft branch: a carpenter's small workshop.
branches.cn: 手艺分支：木匠的小作坊。

branches.en: The repair branch: a bus back with a broken door.
branches.cn: 修理分支：车门坏了回厂的车。

branches.en: The class branch: a Saturday writing workshop.
branches.cn: 课程分支：周六的写作工作坊。

branches.en: The specialist branch: six teachers drafting a course.
branches.cn: 专家分支：六位老师起草课程。

branches.en: The making branch: both rooms are places where something is made.
branches.cn: 制作分支：两种场景都是做出东西的地方。

intro.en: Workshop is a plain compound of two native words, with no living suffix at all.
intro.cn: workshop 是两个本土语的简单复合，完全没有活的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Neither element is Latin; the words below were borrowed from Latin for the same places of work.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都不是拉丁语；下面的词是从拉丁语借来表示同样工作场所的。

items.meaning: a place of working or trade

items.example: A word of Latin origin for the same idea.
items.exampleCN: 同义而源自拉丁语的词。
它构成 laboratory 与 factory。

items.example: Latin seed, now the nearest word to sense 03.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语的种子，如今最接近第 3 义。

definition_zh: 虫；蠕虫；蚯蚓；蠕动着前进；逐步套取（消息）
definition_en: a small soft creature with a long thin body and no legs, or to move slowly by twisting like one
core_image: 一块翻开的湿土里，一条细长的身体一缩一伸地往前移
scene: 雨后的小路上，几条蚯蚓被水冲出来，在石头上慢慢扭。The dog wormed its way under the gate and was gone before anyone noticed.
sceneCN: 这里 worm 是「虫、蠕虫」（第 1 个义项：身体细长柔软、没有腿的小生物）；句意为那条狗从大门底下钻了过去，谁也没注意到它就没了影。湿土里一缩一伸的细长身体，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 worm 加 -y 构成，义为「多虫的；虫蛀的」
由 worm 加 -like 构成，义为「像虫的；细长的」
由 silk 与 worm 复合，义为「蚕」

senses.title: The legless creature
senses.definition: a small soft animal with a long thin body and no legs, living in soil or water
senses.definitionCN: 身体细长柔软、没有腿的小动物，生活在土里或水中
senses.example: After the rain the worms came up and lay on the path.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后虫子钻出土来，躺在小路上。
senses.why: This is the creature itself, the shape of which drives every other sense.
senses.whyCN: 这就是这种生物本身，它的形状驱动了其余所有义项。

senses.title: To move like one
senses.definition: to move slowly and with difficulty by twisting the body close to the ground
senses.definitionCN: 贴着地扭动身体，缓慢艰难地移动
senses.example: The dog wormed its way under the gate and was gone before anyone noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗从大门底下钻了过去，谁也没注意到它就没影了。
senses.why: The verb borrows the body's way of travelling: no legs, no hurry, just twisting forward.
senses.whyCN: 动词借用了这种身体的走法：没有腿，也不急，只是一路扭过去。

senses.title: To pull secrets out bit by bit
senses.definition: to get information out of someone slowly and indirectly, as in worm something out of someone
senses.definitionCN: 慢慢间接地从他人那里取得消息，如 worm something out of someone
senses.example: It took her an hour to worm the truth out of him.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了一个小时才从他嘴里套出实情。
senses.why: Wriggling into a narrow place is exactly how one gets into another person's confidence step by step.
senses.whyCN: 往窄缝里慢慢钻，正是人一步步钻进别人心事里的样子。

senses.title: The wretched person
senses.definition: a mean and contemptible person, used as a word of low abuse
senses.definitionCN: 卑劣可鄙的人，用作轻蔑的骂词
senses.example: Nobody trusted the worm who had sold the plans to a rival.
senses.exampleCN: 没人信任那个把图纸卖给对手的可鄙家伙。
senses.why: A creature that lives by creeping and twisting easily becomes a picture of a person who betrays.
senses.whyCN: 靠钻营扭动过活的生物，很容易变成背叛者的画像。

senses.title: The one who turns at last
senses.definition: used in the saying the worm turns, meaning even the most patient person will resist
senses.definitionCN: 用于谚语 the worm turns，意即最忍让的人也会反抗
senses.example: He said nothing for years, and then the worm turned.
senses.exampleCN: 他多年不作声，后来终于翻脸了。
senses.why: Even a body with no strength can turn, and that turning is the proverb's whole point.
senses.whyCN: 就连毫无力气的身体也能扭过来，这个「扭」就是整句谚语的要点。

intro.en: Worm is Old English wyrm, which first meant a serpent, and only later narrowed to the small creatures of soil.
intro.cn: worm 来自古英语 wyrm，最初指蛇，后来才收窄为土里的小虫。

items.en: wyrm meant a snake or a dragon, the long bending body, not the small soil creature.
items.cn: wyrm 指蛇或龙，是那细长扭动的身体，并非土中小虫。

items.en: The same word for serpent appears in Norse and German forms.
items.cn: 表示蛇的同一词出现在北欧与德语的形式中。

items.en: Latin vermis, a worm, lived beside it in learned writing and reinforced the small-creature sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vermis（虫）在学术写作中与之并存，强化了小虫之义。

items.en: The meaning narrowed to small soft creatures, while dragon survived only in old poetry.
items.cn: 词义收窄为柔软的小生物，龙义仅存于古诗。

items.en: The verb grew out of the creature's way of moving, and then out of its way of getting in.
items.cn: 动词先由它移动的方式长出来，再延伸到它钻进去的方式。

note.en: The first group holds the derived forms, the second holds other small creatures that people confuse it with.
note.cn: 第一组收派生形式，第二组收容易与它混淆的其他小生物。

entries.definition: More than one worm.
Full of worms, or eaten by them.
The caterpillar that spins silk.
A small creature with six legs and a body in three parts.
A long thin animal with no legs and scales.
The wormlike young of a butterfly or moth.

normalIntro.en: Worm is a short old word whose first meaning was snake, and whose shape still drives its metaphors.
normalIntro.cn: worm 是一个短小的古词，最初指蛇，它的形状至今驱动着各种比喻。

normal.en: Worm rhymes with term, and unlike warm it keeps a short crisp vowel.
normal.cn: worm 与 term 押韵，与 warm 不同，元音短而紧。

normal.en: The first meaning was snake, so a worm in old texts may be something larger.
normal.cn: 最初义是蛇，所以旧文本里的 worm 可能是个更大的东西。

normal.en: Silkworm and tapeworm show the word joining with another to name a kind.
normal.cn: silkworm 与 tapeworm 显示它与另一词结合来指某一类。

normal.en: Worm out of means pull out slowly, like a thread pulled by twisting.
normal.cn: worm out of 指慢悠悠地拽出来，像扭着拉一根线。

normal.en: The worm turns comes from the idea that even a soft body will finally wriggle free.
normal.cn: the worm turns 源自「再软的身体最后也会扭开」的想象。

abstract.en: A thin body folding and unfolding through wet soil.
abstract.cn: 细长的身体在湿土里一折一伸。

abstract.en: A shape with no eyes, no legs, and no pause.
abstract.cn: 一个没有眼睛、没有腿、也不停下的形状。

abstract.en: A body that moves by giving up its own straightness.
abstract.cn: 一个靠放弃笔直而前进的身体。

examples.en: The child put the worm back into the soil gently.
examples.cn: 孩子轻轻把蚯蚓放回土里。

examples.en: He wormed through the narrow gap behind the shelf.
examples.cn: 他从架子后面的窄缝里挤了过去。

examples.en: She wormed the whole story out of her brother at dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭时她把整件事从弟弟嘴里套了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我摸」——土里一摸，摸到一条软软的虫。

root: 古英语 wyrm（蛇；龙），与德语、北欧语同源；拉丁语 vermis（虫）在后世加强「小虫」义。

sensesIntro.en: The creature comes first, then its way of moving, then its way of creeping into secrets, then the abuse, and finally the revolt.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是这种生物，再是它移动的样子，接着是它钻进秘密的方式，然后是骂人语，最后是反抗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin body folding through wet soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿土里一折一伸的细长身体。

branches.en: The creature branch: worms lying on the path after rain.
branches.cn: 生物分支：雨后躺在路上的虫。

branches.en: The movement branch: a dog wriggling under the gate.
branches.cn: 移动分支：从门下钻过的狗。

branches.en: The secret branch: pulling the truth out slowly.
branches.cn: 秘密分支：慢慢套出实情。

branches.en: The abuse branch: the one who sold the plans.
branches.cn: 骂词分支：卖图纸的那个人。

branches.en: The revolt branch: silence that finally breaks.
branches.cn: 反抗分支：终于打破的沉默。

intro.en: Worm is a bare stem; -y and -like build adjectives, and compounds name whole families of creatures.
intro.cn: worm 是裸词干；-y 与 -like 构成形容词，复合词则命名一整类生物。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, but Latin vermis lived beside it and left its own traces, such as vermin.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，但拉丁语 vermis 与之并存，并留下了 vermin 之类的痕迹。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 vermin 与 vermicelli。

definition_zh: 值得做的；值得花时间的；值得花力气的；有价值的
definition_en: worth the time, effort or money spent on it
core_image: 一趟跋涉之后站在山顶，疲劳还在，心里却说不虚此行
scene: 花了三年改稿，书终于出版，作者说这三年没白费。It is worthwhile checking the figures before you send the report.
sceneCN: 这里 worthwhile 是「值得做的」（第 1 个义项：花的时间与力气有回报）；句意为发报告前把数据核一遍是值得的。爬到山顶说不虚此行的感觉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：值得做的、值得花时间的、值得花力气的

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「价值」，是合成词的前半部分
名词，义为「一段时间」，是合成词的后半部分
副词，义为「无价值地」，属反面一支
形容词，义为「值得的、可敬的」，同族
介词，义为「值、值得」，常与 doing 连用

senses.title: Worth the time given
senses.titleCN: 值得做：花掉的时间有回报
senses.definition: worth the time spent on it
senses.definitionCN: 花在上面的时间有回报
senses.example: It is worthwhile checking the figures before you send the report.
senses.exampleCN: 发报告前把数据核一遍是值得的。
senses.why: The word joins worth, value, to while, a stretch of time: the value must cover the time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 worth「价值」与 while「一段时间」拼在一起：价值必须抵得过时间。

senses.title: Worth the effort
senses.titleCN: 值得费力：辛苦没有白费
senses.definition: worth the effort and difficulty involved
senses.definitionCN: 付出的力气与困难有回报
senses.example: The climb was hard, but the view made it worthwhile.
senses.exampleCN: 爬山很辛苦，但风景让这趟很值。
senses.why: Effort is a cost like money, and the word can be paid in it too.
senses.whyCN: 力气是和金钱一样的成本，这个词也接受用力气付款。

senses.title: Worth the money
senses.titleCN: 值得花钱：投入能收回来
senses.definition: worth the money paid for it
senses.definitionCN: 付出的钱能收回来
senses.example: The repairs were expensive but worthwhile in the long run.
senses.exampleCN: 修理费很贵，但长远看是值得的。
senses.why: Cost and benefit sit in the same sentence, and the word decides for the benefit.
senses.whyCN: 成本与收益被放进同一个句子，而这个词判给了收益。

senses.title: Worth doing at all
senses.titleCN: 有价值的：事情本身有意义
senses.definition: having real value or importance, said of causes and work
senses.definitionCN: 本身具有真实价值，用于事业与工作
senses.example: She found the work worthwhile even though the pay was low.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得这份工作很有意义，尽管报酬很低。
senses.why: Here the return is not money but meaning, the widest kind of while that worth can cover.
senses.whyCN: 这里的回报不是钱而是意义，这是 worth 能抵付的最宽的一种时间。

intro.en: Worthwhile is a late English compound: worth, value, plus while, a period of time, meaning worth the time.
intro.cn: worthwhile 是较晚出现的英语合成词：worth「价值」加 while「一段时间」，即「值这段时间」。

items.en: The noun weorth meant value or price, and the preposition use came later.
items.cn: 名词 weorth 意为价值或价钱，介词用法出现较晚。

items.en: The noun hwil meant a period of time, source of modern while.
items.cn: 名词 hwil 意为一段时间，是现代 while 的来源。

items.en: Worthwhile appeared as a compound in the nineteenth century, first in American writing.
items.cn: worthwhile 作为合成词在十九世纪出现，最早见于美国文字。

items.en: Modern usage often follows worth one’s while and it is worthwhile doing.
items.cn: 现代用法常见 worth one’s while 与 it is worthwhile doing 两种句式。

items.en: The word spread from business and education into general judgements of effort.
items.cn: 这个词从商业与教育扩展到对一切付出的总体评价。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the worth- family and the while compound; the near-meaning group holds words for being worth something.
note.cn: 形近组沿 worth- 家族与 while 合成词；近义组收表示值得的词。

entries.definition: Value, or the preposition meaning deserving of.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或介词，义为「价值、值得」，本词前半部。

entries.definition: A period of time; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一段时间」，本词后半部。

entries.definition: Deserving of respect or effort, used of people and causes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得的、可敬的」，用于人与事业。

entries.definition: Having no value, the negative cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无价值的」，反面的近亲。

entries.definition: Worth a lot, often in money or usefulness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有价值的」，多指金钱或效用。

entries.definition: Giving satisfaction for the effort made.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有回报的」，强调满足感。

entries.definition: Helpful for a purpose, without the cost comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有用的」，不含成本比较。

entries.definition: Not worth doing at all, the opposite judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毫无意义的」，相反的判断。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal sum inside the compound: value versus time spent.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用合成词里那笔字面账：价值对花掉的时间。

normal.en: Worthwhile is worth plus while: the value must cover the time.
normal.cn: worthwhile 是 worth 加 while：价值要抵得住时间。

normal.en: It is worthwhile doing is the standard pattern before a gerund.
normal.cn: worthwhile 后接动名词时常用 it is worthwhile doing 的句式。

normal.en: Well worthwhile adds emphasis but changes nothing else.
normal.cn: well worthwhile 只是加强语气，其余不变。

normal.en: Worthy describes people and causes, worthwhile describes time and effort.
normal.cn: worthy 说人与事业，worthwhile 说时间与力气。

normal.en: Make it worthwhile means add something so the effort pays.
normal.cn: make it worthwhile 指加点东西让这份辛苦有回报。

abstract.en: The compound hides an economics of life: every yes to one thing is a no to the hours it takes.
abstract.cn: 这个合成词藏着一门生活经济学：对一件事说「好」，就是对它占用的钟点说「不」。

abstract.en: Value here is judged afterwards as well as before; that is why we say it proved worthwhile.
abstract.cn: 这里的价值既在事前判断也在事后判断，所以说 it proved worthwhile。

abstract.en: Anything worth the while is worth it to someone, which is why the word never settles a question by itself.
abstract.cn: 值不值总是对某个人而言，所以这个词从不能独自断案。

examples.en: It is worthwhile keeping a copy of every letter.
examples.cn: 每封信都留个副本是值得的。

examples.en: The extra training proved worthwhile in the end.
examples.cn: 额外的培训最终证明是值得的。

examples.en: They made the trip worthwhile by staying an extra week.
examples.cn: 他们多待了一周，让这趟行程更值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃思外偶」——沃思（我思）外偶（外哦），外面走走也值得：值得做的

root: 由 worth「价值」与 while「一段时间」在十九世纪合成，意为「值得花这段时间的」；同族词有 worth、worthy、worthless。

sensesIntro.en: Worthwhile measures the return on time, effort, money, or the plain value of the work itself.
sensesIntro.cn: worthwhile 衡量的是对时间、力气、金钱的回报，或工作本身的价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing on a summit, tired but certain the climb was not wasted.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在山顶，累却确定这趟没白爬。

branches.en: TIME LINE: hours spent and repaid.
branches.cn: 时间线：花掉的钟点被偿还。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the effort paid off.
branches.cn: 身体线：力气有了回报。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the cost comes back.
branches.cn: 金钱线：成本收得回来。

branches.en: MEANING LINE: the work matters in itself.
branches.cn: 意义线：工作本身就有价值。

branches.en: CONTRAST: worthwhile is about return, worthy is about merit.
branches.cn: 对照线：worthwhile 讲回报，worthy 讲品格。

intro.en: Worthwhile is a compound of two whole English words; nothing is glued on with an affix.
intro.cn: worthwhile 是两个完整英语词的合成，没有使用词缀粘接。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin here; both halves are Old English nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分，前后两半都是古英语名词。

items.example: It forms worthwhileness in rare use.
It appears in older forms of the compound.
It is the full phrase behind it.
items.exampleCN: 它是本词背后的完整说法。

definition_zh: 值得的；配得上的；可敬的；有价值的
definition_en: deserving something good, or having enough merit to be respected
core_image: 一件旧外套洗得发白、补过两次，但穿它的人站得很直
scene: 评选名单上，那个默默做了十年杂事的人排在最前面。Her work with the children is worthy of more attention than it gets.
sceneCN: 这里 worthy 是「值得的、配得上的」（第 1 个义项：理应得到某种好的对待）；句意为她为孩子们所做的工作理应得到更多关注，而实际得到的太少。洗得发白却站得笔直的旧外套，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 要人；知名人士（多带调侃）

derivatives.zh: 由 worthy 加 -ness 构成，义为「值得；可贵之处」
由 worthy 加 -ly 构成，义为「值得地；相称地」
由 worthy 加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不值得的；不相称的」
由 praise 与 worthy 复合，义为「值得称赞的」

senses.title: Deserving of something
senses.definition: having enough value to deserve a particular good thing, as in worthy of praise
senses.definitionCN: 有价值到理应得到某种好的对待，如 worthy of praise
senses.example: Her work with the children is worthy of more attention than it gets.
senses.exampleCN: 她为孩子们所做的工作理应得到更多关注，而实际得到的太少。
senses.why: The root is worth, so the adjective says a person or thing has enough value to deserve its reward.
senses.whyCN: 词根是 worth，所以这个形容词表示某人某物有足够价值，理应得到那份回报。

senses.title: Respectable in itself
senses.definition: having the qualities that earned respect, often used of effort and character
senses.definitionCN: 具备赢来尊敬的那些品质，常用于努力与品性
senses.example: It is a worthy attempt even if it did not succeed.
senses.exampleCN: 即使没有成功，这也是一次可敬的尝试。
senses.why: The frame worthy of can drop its object, leaving the sense that the effort itself carries merit.
senses.whyCN: worthy of 的句式可以省去对象，留下「这份努力本身就有价值」的意思。

senses.title: The local notable
senses.definition: used as a noun, often with a touch of mockery, for a local person of standing
senses.definitionCN: 作名词用，常带一点调侃，指地方上有地位的人
senses.example: The town worthies gathered on the platform to give short speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的头面人物都聚到台上做简短的讲话。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for people who are thought to embody worth, and the tone turns dry.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指被认为有分量的人，语气随之带上了干涩的调侃。

senses.title: Worth the trouble
senses.definition: used of a cause or a thing that justifies the effort put into it
senses.definitionCN: 用于值得为之付出的事业或事物
senses.example: The repair of the old bridge is a worthy cause for the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 重修这座老桥是对整个村子都值得的一件事。
senses.why: Applied to a cause, the word answers the question whether the effort will be repaid.
senses.whyCN: 用到一件事上时，这个词回答的是「这份力气会不会有回报」。

intro.en: Worthy is Old English weorthig, worth plus the adjective ending -ig, then -y in modern spelling.
intro.cn: worthy 来自古英语 weorthig，即 worth 加形容词词尾 -ig，现代拼写变为 -y。

items.en: The adjective weorthig said that a thing had worth and so deserved regard.
items.cn: 形容词 weorthig 表示某物有价值，因而值得看重。

items.en: The ending weakened, giving worthy, and the noun use appeared.
items.cn: 词尾弱化，形成 worthy，名词用法也随之出现。

items.en: Worthy of became the standard frame for saying what is deserved.
items.cn: worthy of 成了表示「配得上」的标准句式。

items.en: In speech the adjective can sound a little stiff, which is why self-made uses poke fun.
items.cn: 口语中这个形容词略显板正，所以有些用法是拿来打趣的。

items.en: Unworthy and praiseworthy show how freely the word compounds.
items.cn: unworthy 与 praiseworthy 说明这个词复合得多么自由。

note.en: The first group holds the family around worth, the second holds adjectives of deserving and of respect.
note.cn: 第一组收 worth 周围的家族词，第二组收表示值得与可敬的形容词。

entries.definition: Value, or deserving of something.
The quality of deserving respect.
Not deserving, or not good enough.
Having earned good treatment.
Deserving respect and approval.
Of a good social standing, decent.

normalIntro.en: Worthy is worth plus y, with the comparison taking -ier and -iest.
normalIntro.cn: worthy 是 worth 加 -y，比较级和最高级分别用 -ier 与 -iest。

normal.en: The y turns to i in the comparison: worthier and worthiest.
normal.cn: 比较级里 y 变 i：worthier 与 worthiest。

normal.en: Worthy of is the frame: worthy of praise, worthy of note.
normal.cn: 常用框架是 worthy of：worthy of praise、worthy of note。

normal.en: Add un- for the opposite: unworthy of the honour.
normal.cn: 加 un- 得反义：unworthy of the honour。

normal.en: The ringing is voiced here, unlike the th in worth, because the ending is voiced too.
normal.cn: 这里的 th 发浊音，与 worth 的清音不同，因为词尾也是浊音。

normal.en: Praiseworthy and noteworthy are compounds, and both keep the y.
normal.cn: praiseworthy 与 noteworthy 都是复合词，都保留 y。

abstract.en: A coat washed pale and mended twice, worn by someone standing straight.
abstract.cn: 洗得发白、补过两次的外套，穿着它的人站得很直。

abstract.en: A name on a list placed above louder names.
abstract.cn: 名单上的一个名字排在更响的名字之上。

abstract.en: A hand held out to an opponent who fought well.
abstract.cn: 伸手递给一个打得好的对手。

examples.en: The plan is worthy of serious discussion.
examples.cn: 这个方案值得认真讨论。

examples.en: He is a worthy opponent and a fair player.
examples.cn: 他是个值得尊敬的对手，也打得公道。

examples.en: Teaching the children to read is a worthy cause.
examples.cn: 教孩子们读书是一件值得做的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我值」——我「值」得这份尊敬，就是 worthy。

root: 古英语 weorthig = weorth（价值）+ -ig（形容词词尾，今作 -y）；比较级 worthier，反义 unworthy。

sensesIntro.en: Deserving a reward comes first, then being respectable in oneself, then the humorous use as a noun, and finally the cause worth doing for.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是理应得到回报，再是自身可敬，然后是带调侃的名词用法，最后是值得去做的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mended coat worn by someone standing straight.
core.cn: 核心意象：补过的旧外套，穿着的人站得笔直。

branches.en: The deserving branch: work worthy of more attention.
branches.cn: 应得分支：理应得到更多关注的工作。

branches.en: The character branch: a worthy attempt that failed.
branches.cn: 品性分支：失败却可敬的尝试。

branches.en: The noun branch: town worthies giving speeches.
branches.cn: 名词分支：镇上头面人物讲话。

branches.en: The cause branch: repairing the old bridge.
branches.cn: 事业分支：重修老桥。

branches.en: The frame branch: worthy of plus a noun is the usual shape.
branches.cn: 句式分支：常用 worthy of 接名词。

intro.en: Worthy is a stem plus -y, and it still lives by the frame worthy of.
intro.cn: worthy 是词干加 -y，至今仍活在 worthy of 这个句式里。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin words below express deserving with a different verb.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语；下面的拉丁词用另一个动词表达「值得」。

definition_zh: 包；裹；缠绕；围住；（使）结束；（电影）拍完
definition_en: to cover something by folding paper or cloth around it, or to wind something around; also to finish an activity
core_image: 把东西放进去，四角折过来，一条细绳绕三圈系住
scene: 生日前夜，桌上摆着剪好的纸和一卷彩色带子，礼物还露着一角。She wrapped the bowl in newspaper so it would survive the journey.
sceneCN: 这里 wrap 是「包、裹」（第 1 个义项：用纸或布把东西折起来盖住）；句意为她用报纸把碗包好，好让它经得住颠簸。四角折过来、细绳绕三圈，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wrap 加 -er 构成，义为「包装纸；封套」
由 wrap 加 -ing 构成，义为「包装材料」
由 wrap 加 -ed 构成，义为「包好的；入神的」

senses.title: To cover it round
senses.definition: to fold paper or cloth right round a thing so that it is covered on all sides
senses.definitionCN: 把纸或布整个折起来围住某物，使其四面都被盖住
senses.example: She wrapped the bowl in newspaper so it would survive the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 她用报纸把碗包好，好让它经得住颠簸。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to wind cloth around something, and every other sense is that motion again.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是把布绕在东西上，其余义项都是这个动作的再现。

senses.title: To wind round and round
senses.definition: to put something such as a band or a cord round a thing several times
senses.definitionCN: 把带子、绳子之类在物体上绕好几圈
senses.example: A thin ribbon was wrapped twice around the box.
senses.exampleCN: 一条细带子在盒子上绕了两圈。
senses.why: The same motion is now used with a cord instead of a sheet, so the word still means to circle a thing.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作换成绳而不是布，这个词仍然是把东西绕起来。

senses.title: To finish something
senses.definition: to bring an activity, a meeting or a filming to its end, as in wrap up
senses.definitionCN: 让一项活动、会议或拍摄告一段落，如 wrap up
senses.example: Let us wrap up the meeting before the train leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 咱们趁火车开走之前把会开完。
senses.why: When work is wrapped up, the last loose ends are folded in as if they were being covered, and then the whole is closed.
senses.whyCN: 把工作「包完」，就是把最后几处散头折进去，像盖住一样，然后把整体合上。

senses.title: To be absorbed in something
senses.definition: to give all one's attention to something, as in wrapped up in
senses.definitionCN: 把全部注意力放在某事上，如 wrapped up in
senses.example: He was so wrapped up in his book that he missed his stop.
senses.exampleCN: 他看得太入神，坐过了站。
senses.why: Attention wound tightly around one subject leaves nothing outside, so a person inside a book is wrapped in it.
senses.whyCN: 注意力紧紧绕在一个主题上，外面就什么都不剩，于是埋头读书的人便是被书「裹住」了。

intro.en: Wrap is of uncertain origin, appearing in Middle English as wrappen, and probably related to the older sense of turning and rolling.
intro.cn: wrap 的词源不确定，中古英语作 wrappen，可能与其更早的「翻转、滚卷」之意相关。

items.en: wrappen meant to wind or to fold a covering round something.
items.cn: wrappen 意为缠绕或用覆布把某物包起来。

items.en: No older Germanic form is certainly related, and its ancestry is still argued.
items.cn: 没有确定的更早日耳曼语形式与之相关，其渊源至今仍有争议。

items.en: The ending -er built wrapper for the paper and the cover.
items.cn: 后缀 -er 造出 wrapper，指包装纸与封套。

items.en: The sense to finish grew in American film making, where a shot was wrapped.
items.cn: 「结束」这一义项在美国电影制作中生长出来，镜头拍完就叫 wrapped。

items.en: The phrase under wraps, kept secret, comes from cloth keeping a thing hidden.
items.cn: under wraps（保密）来自用布把东西盖住藏起来。

note.en: The first group holds the derived forms, the second holds other verbs for covering and binding.
note.cn: 第一组收派生形式，第二组收其他表示包裹与捆扎的动词。

entries.definition: Covered, or wholly absorbed in something.
The paper or cover around a thing.
Material used for wrapping.
To put something over a thing.
To tie or fasten together.
To bend something over on itself.

normalIntro.en: Wrap ends in a single p, but doubles it before a vowel ending: wrapped, wrapping.
normalIntro.cn: wrap 末尾只有一个 p，但在元音词尾前要双写：wrapped、wrapping。

normal.en: Double the p before -ed and -ing: wrapped and wrapping, not wraped.
normal.cn: -ed 与 -ing 前双写 p：wrapped、wrapping，而不是 wraped。

normal.en: The past tense is wrapped, not wraped, because wrap is a one-syllable word ending in p.
normal.cn: 过去式是 wrapped，因为 wrap 是单音节且以 p 结尾。

normal.en: Wrap up means both to cover and to finish, so context decides.
normal.cn: wrap up 既指包起来也指结束，看上下文定。

normal.en: Under wraps means hidden from everyone, like a gift before the day.
normal.cn: under wraps 指藏起来不让知道，如节前的礼物。

normal.en: Rap is the look-alike with one p, meaning to knock; wrap with w covers.
normal.cn: 单写 p 的 rap 是敲击；带 w 的 wrap 是包裹。

abstract.en: Four corners folded in, then a string wound three times.
abstract.cn: 四角折进来，再绕三圈绳。

abstract.en: A gift still showing one corner of paper.
abstract.cn: 礼物还露着一角纸。

abstract.en: A person so inside a book that the world outside stops.
abstract.cn: 一个人陷在书里，外面的世界停了。

examples.en: Please wrap the glasses in paper before packing them.
examples.cn: 装之前请把杯子用纸包一下。

examples.en: We should wrap up the report before Friday.
examples.cn: 我们应该在周五之前把报告收尾。

examples.en: The present is still under wraps until his birthday.
examples.cn: 礼物到他生日之前一直保密。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「绕」——把东西一绕一包，就是 wrap。

root: 中古英语 wrappen（缠绕、包覆），更早来源不确定；加 -ed、-ing 时双写 p；-er 构成 wrapper。

sensesIntro.en: The cloth goes round the thing, then the cord winds round it, then the session is wound up, and finally attention is wound around one subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是布绕上东西，再是绳绕上东西，接着是把一场活动绕完，最后是把注意力绕在一件事上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four corners folded in, a string wound three times.
core.cn: 核心意象：四角折入，绳绕三圈。

branches.en: The covering branch: a bowl wrapped in newspaper.
branches.cn: 包裹分支：用报纸包起的碗。

branches.en: The winding branch: ribbon wrapped twice around a box.
branches.cn: 缠绕分支：绕了两圈的带子。

branches.en: The ending branch: wrapping up a meeting before a train.
branches.cn: 结束分支：赶火车前把会开完。

branches.en: The absorption branch: too deep in a book to notice the stop.
branches.cn: 专注分支：看书入神坐过站。

branches.en: The privacy branch: kept under wraps, like a covered gift.
branches.cn: 隐秘分支：像盖住的礼物一样保密。

intro.en: Wrap is a short stem with a doubled p before endings, and -er and -ing build its nouns.
intro.cn: wrap 是短词干，词尾前双写 p，-er 与 -ing 构成其名词。

latinIntro.en: The stem has no Latin ancestor; the words below cover the same action from the Latin side.
latinIntro.cn: 词干没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词从拉丁语一侧表达同样的动作。

definition_zh: 失事的船；残骸；事故；毁坏；使（船）失事
definition_en: a ship or vehicle destroyed in an accident, the broken remains of it, or to destroy something completely
core_image: 退潮后的沙滩上，一艘龙骨断裂的船半埋进沙里
scene: 风暴过后的清晨，海边的浅滩上躺着一艘只剩骨架的船。Divers found a wreck from the last century near the harbour mouth.
sceneCN: 这里 wreck 是「失事的船；残骸」（第 1 个义项：在事故中被毁的船或车，以及它剩下的残骸）；句意为潜水员在港口入口附近发现一艘上个世纪失事的船。退潮沙滩上那艘断了龙骨的船，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wreck 加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「残骸；碎片」
由 wreck 加施动后缀 -er 构成，义为「打捞船的人；拆毁者」
由 wreck 加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「失事的；被毁的」

senses.title: The broken ship
senses.definition: a ship, car, or plane that has been badly damaged or destroyed in an accident, or what is left of it
senses.definitionCN: 在事故中严重损坏或被毁的船、车或飞机，也指其残骸
senses.example: Divers found a wreck from the last century near the harbour mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员在港口入口附近发现一艘上个世纪失事的船。
senses.why: Wreck first named a ship driven onto rocks and broken, so the object that survives an accident came to be called by its story.
senses.whyCN: wreck 最初指被风浪推上礁石撞碎的船，于是「经历事故后剩下的东西」就用这个故事的名称来称呼。

senses.title: The crash itself
senses.definition: an accident in which a vehicle is badly damaged or someone is badly hurt
senses.definitionCN: 车辆严重损坏或有人受重伤的事故
senses.example: The road was closed for hours after a wreck involving three trucks.
senses.exampleCN: 三辆卡车相撞的事故后，那条路封闭了几个小时。
senses.why: Because a broken hull is the visible result of a crash, the word moved from the result to the event that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 因为破碎的船体是撞毁事件看得见的结果，这个词就从结果移到了造成结果的事件上。

senses.title: A person in pieces
senses.definition: someone whose health, nerves, or life has been ruined, often in the phrase a nervous wreck
senses.definitionCN: 健康、精神或生活被摧毁的人，常见于说法 a nervous wreck
senses.example: After two sleepless nights she was a nervous wreck.
senses.exampleCN: 两个不眠之夜后，她的精神彻底垮了。
senses.why: If a body can be broken like a ship on rocks, then the same image describes a person whose nerves have cracked.
senses.whyCN: 如果身体可以像触礁的船一样被撞碎，那么同一个意象就能形容精神开裂的人。

senses.title: To break something apart
senses.definition: to damage or destroy something completely, or to cause a ship to break up
senses.definitionCN: 彻底损坏或摧毁某物，或使船破裂失事
senses.example: The storm wrecked two fishing boats on the same night.
senses.exampleCN: 那一夜风暴让两条渔船失事。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to give something the fate of the broken ship is to wreck it.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了动词：让某物遭遇破船的命运，就是 wreck it。

senses.title: The ruined plan
senses.definition: to spoil or ruin something such as a plan, a chance, or a relationship
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、机会或关系等破灭或遭到破坏
senses.example: Heavy rain wrecked our plans for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨毁了我们的野餐计划。
senses.why: Abstract things are treated like fragile vessels, so whatever breaks them is said to wreck them.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的东西被当作易碎的容器，于是毁掉它们就说成 wreck。

intro.en: Wreck came into English from Old Norse and is related to the idea of something driven ashore and broken; the modern noun and verb grew from that picture.
intro.cn: wreck 由古诺斯语进入英语，本义与被冲上岸、撞碎的东西有关；现代的名词与动词都是从这幅画面长出来的。

items.en: The verb rekja and the noun wreck meant to drive something, especially a ship, ashore.
items.cn: 动词 rekja 与名词 wreck 意为把东西（尤指船）冲到岸上。

items.en: wrak or wrek named goods and ships cast up on the shore after a storm.
items.cn: wrak 或 wrek 指风暴后冲上岸的货物与船只。

items.en: Coastal law spoke of wreckum, the right to claim what the sea threw up.
items.cn: 沿海法律里说 wreckum，指认领大海抛上岸之物的权利。

items.en: The meaning widened from stranded ships to any vehicle or person that has been ruined.
items.cn: 词义从搁浅的船扩大到任何被毁的车辆或人。

items.en: The verb to wreck, meaning to ruin, is a later back-formation from the noun.
items.cn: 表示毁坏的动词 wreck 是由名词后期反向构成的。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same seamanship family, the second holds other words for ruin and disaster.
note.cn: 第一组收同一航海词族里的词，第二组收其他表示毁灭与灾难的词。

entries.definition: The broken parts left after a wreck.
A person or vehicle that clears away wrecks.
Destroyed or badly damaged.
To spoil or destroy something completely.
Scattered pieces left after something is destroyed.
The body of an old or broken ship.

normalIntro.en: Wreck is one syllable and starts with wr, the old English spelling habit that keeps the r silent.
normalIntro.cn: wreck 只有一个音节，以 wr 开头，这是英语里 r 不发音的老拼写习惯。

normal.en: The wr at the start is silent in the r, as in write and wrong.
normal.cn: 开头的 wr 里 r 不发音，write 与 wrong 也是这样。

normal.en: The same word gives shipwreck and wreckage.
normal.cn: 同一个词构成 shipwreck 与 wreckage。

normal.en: A nervous wreck borrows the image of a ship broken on rocks.
normal.cn: nervous wreck 借的是触礁碎船的意象。

normal.en: Wreck as a verb means to ruin, as in wreck the plan.
normal.cn: wreck 作动词意为毁掉，如 wreck the plan。

normal.en: Wreck is related to the Old Norse verb rekja, to drive ashore.
normal.cn: wreck 与古诺斯语动词 rekja（冲上岸）有关。

abstract.en: A broken keel sticking out of wet sand at low tide.
abstract.cn: 退潮时从湿沙里露出的断裂龙骨。

abstract.en: The silence after the wave has finished throwing things around.
abstract.cn: 浪把东西抛完之后的那片安静。

abstract.en: Something that once moved now lying still in pieces.
abstract.cn: 曾经会动的东西如今碎着躺下不动。

examples.en: The wreck of an old fishing boat was still visible at low tide.
examples.cn: 退潮时仍能看见一艘旧渔船的残骸。

examples.en: Two drivers were hurt in the wreck on the motorway.
examples.cn: 高速公路上的车祸中有两名司机受伤。

examples.en: The storm wrecked the harbour wall and flooded the village.
examples.cn: 风暴毁坏了码头墙，淹了村子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来克」——礁石来克船，船就被克得只剩骨架。

root: 源自中古英语 wrak、wrek，来自古诺斯语 *wrek，本义为「被冲上岸的东西、漂来的残骸」，与 rekja（冲、赶）同源；同族词有 wreckage、wrecked。

sensesIntro.en: The broken ship comes first, then the crash that broke it, then the ruined person, then the act of ruining anything, then ruined plans.
sensesIntro.cn: 先有破碎的船，再有撞碎它的事故，然后是垮掉的人，接着是毁掉任何东西的动作，最后是破灭的计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broken hull half buried in sand.
core.cn: 核心意象：半埋在沙里的破碎船体。

branches.en: The object branch: what is left of the ship.
branches.cn: 实物分支：船剩下的东西。

branches.en: The event branch: the crash that produced the wreck.
branches.cn: 事件分支：造成残骸的那场撞毁。

branches.en: The human branch: a body broken like a ship.
branches.cn: 人分支：像船一样被撞碎的身体。

branches.en: The action branch: giving something the fate of a ship on rocks.
branches.cn: 动作分支：让某物经历触礁的船那样的命运。

branches.en: The image branch: both a ship and a person can end up in pieces.
branches.cn: 意象分支：船和人最后都可能碎成一堆。

intro.en: Wreck is a free stem borrowed from Old Norse; English added -age, -er and -ed to build the family around it.
intro.cn: wreck 是从古诺斯语借入的自由词干，英语在它周围加上 -age、-er、-ed 建成词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Norse, not Latin, so no Latin ancestor exists; the entries below are distant Indo-European cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自诺斯语而非拉丁语，因此没有拉丁语祖先；下面几条只是印欧语系的远亲。

items.meaning: the broken ship and the act of breaking
items.meaningCN: 破碎的船与毁坏的动作
items.example: The stem carries both the object and the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干同时承载物与动作。

items.example: Ship names the vessel and wreck names its fate.
items.exampleCN: ship 指明船只，wreck 指明它的命运。

items.meaning: a mass or collection of things
items.example: It forms wreckage, the mass of broken parts.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wreckage，指成堆的残骸。

items.example: It forms wrecker, one who clears wrecks.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrecker，清理残骸的人。

items.example: It forms wrecked, having been destroyed.
The wrecked car blocked the lane.
items.exampleCN: 被撞毁的车堵住了车道。

items.meaning: the act of destroying or the moment of a crash
items.meaningCN: 毁坏的动作或撞毁的时刻
items.example: They cleared the wrecking site at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 他们在黎明时清理了撞毁现场。

items.example: It is a different second element, but the sound recalls wreck.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分是不同的词，但读音让人想起 wreck。

definition_zh: 产出、出产（粮食、收成）；屈服、让步；让路（交通）；名词：产量、收益
definition_en: to produce a crop or result, to give way, or the amount produced
core_image: 一棵压弯了枝的苹果树，果子垂到人手里
scene: 公路口立着一块牌子：前方施工，请让行。These fields yield two crops a year.
sceneCN: 这里 yield 是「出产」（第 1 个义项：田里长出作物）；句意为这些田地一年出产两季作物。被果子压弯的树枝，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：出产、产生；屈服、让步；让路；弯曲、塌陷
名词：产量、收成；收益、利润率

collocations.phrase: give way / yield the right of way

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「柔软的；顺从的；出产的」
在 yielding 后加 -ly，义为「柔顺地」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不屈的、坚硬的」
近义词，义为「产量」，侧重产出量而非动作

senses.title: To produce from the land
senses.definition: to produce a crop, a natural product or a result
senses.definitionCN: 生产出作物、天然产物或结果
senses.example: The orchard yields a good crop of pears each autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这片果园每年秋天都出产好收成。
senses.why: The oldest sense is of the earth giving its fruit; the ground hands over what it grew.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是土地献出果实：土地把长出来的东西交出来。

senses.title: To give way
senses.definition: to stop resisting and accept what is stronger
senses.definitionCN: 停止抵抗，接受更强的一方
senses.example: The government finally yielded to public pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 政府最终屈服于公众压力。
senses.why: From giving fruit, the word moved to giving ground: a defended position is handed over to the opponent.
senses.whyCN: 从献出果实到让出地面：防守的阵地被交给对手。

senses.title: To let others pass
senses.titleCN: 让行：交通中让别人先过
senses.definition: to allow other traffic to go first
senses.definitionCN: 在交通中让别人先行
senses.example: Cars must yield to pedestrians at this crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个路口，车辆必须给行人让行。
senses.why: This is the road version of giving way: one driver hands over the right to move first.
senses.whyCN: 这是「让」的道路版本：一位司机把先行的权利交出去。

senses.title: The amount produced
senses.definition: the quantity produced, as of crops or goods
senses.definitionCN: 出产的数量，如作物或产品
senses.example: Farmers worried about a lower rice yield this year.
senses.exampleCN: 农民担心今年水稻产量降低。
senses.why: The noun simply measures the verb: how much the land or the machine gave over.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是在度量动词：土地或机器交出了多少。

senses.title: The return on money
senses.definition: the profit or income produced by an investment
senses.definitionCN: 投资所产生的利润或收入
senses.example: The bond offers a yield of four percent.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券提供百分之四的收益率。
senses.why: Money, like soil, can be made to yield; the return is the fruit of capital.
senses.whyCN: 钱也像土壤一样能出产；回报就是资本的果实。

senses.title: To bend or give under weight
senses.titleCN: 弯曲、塌陷：在重压下让开
senses.definition: to bend, break or give way under force
senses.definitionCN: 在受力时弯曲、断裂或塌陷
senses.example: The old chair yielded under his weight.
senses.exampleCN: 那把旧椅子在他的重量下塌了下去。
senses.why: Physical giving way: a solid thing stops resisting the load and moves aside.
senses.whyCN: 物理意义上的让：坚固之物不再抵抗重量，让开了。

intro.en: Yield descends from Old English gieldan, a Germanic word for paying what is due.
intro.cn: yield 源自古英语 gieldan，是日耳曼语中表示「付出应付之物」的词。

items.en: Gieldan meant to pay, to repay, or to give up what is owed.
items.cn: Gieldan 意为支付、偿还或交出应付之物。

items.en: The noun gield named a payment or a due amount.
items.cn: 名词 gield 指一笔付款或应付的数额。

items.en: The sense widened from paying money to giving up ground and producing crops.
items.cn: 词义从付钱扩大到让出地面和出产作物。

items.en: In agriculture and trade it settled as the regular word for output and return.
items.cn: 在农业与贸易中，它固定为表示产量与回报的常用词。

items.en: Traffic rules and finance both use it: yield the right of way, and yield on a bond.
items.cn: 交通规则与金融都用它：让行，以及债券的收益率。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers Germanic words with similar spelling and sound; the near-meaning group separates the several senses of giving.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写与读音相似的本土词；近义组按「让」的不同含义区分。

entries.definition: An area of open land; shares the -ield ending but not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「田地」，与 yield 只是尾音相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: A protective piece of armour or a guard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「盾牌、保护」，形状相似。

entries.definition: An old verb meaning to castrate, from the same Germanic base as yield.
entries.definitionCN: 古动词，义为「阉割」，与 yield 同出日耳曼语词干。

entries.definition: An association of craftsmen; spelled alike but a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行会」，拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: To stop fighting and hand over control, more military than yield.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投降、交出」，比 yield 更有军事色彩。

entries.definition: To accept authority or a decision, a more formal yielding.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提交、屈从」，是更正式的让步。

entries.definition: To make or grow something, the plain verb behind sense one.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「生产、生长」，对应第 1 个义项。

entries.definition: The amount made; a neutral noun for yield in industry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「产量」，工业语境里是中性的同义词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the farm picture to the road and the bank.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把田里的画面连到马路和银行。

normal.en: A field that gives fruit yields; the same word gives ground when you yield in traffic.
normal.cn: 出果子的田地叫 yield；在交通里让出地面也是 yield。

normal.en: To yield to pressure is to hand over your resistance like a crop handed over.
normal.cn: 屈服于压力，就像把作物交出去一样交出抵抗。

normal.en: Yield sign at a crossing: you give the right of way, not the argument.
normal.cn: 路口的让行标志：让的是先行权，不是道理。

normal.en: A bond's yield is the fruit of your money.
normal.cn: 债券的 yield 就是你的钱结的果。

normal.en: The old chair yielded: it gave up its shape under him.
normal.cn: 旧椅子 yielded：它在他身下放弃了原来的形状。

abstract.en: One idea under all senses: something holds, then lets go and hands over.
abstract.cn: 所有义项背后只有一个想法：先坚持，然后松手交出。

abstract.en: Earth gives fruit, people give ground, money gives return.
abstract.cn: 土地给果实，人让出地面，钱给出回报。

abstract.en: Picture the bend: a branch loaded with apples leans down to your hand.
abstract.cn: 想那个弯曲：挂满苹果的枝条弯到你的手边。

examples.en: The new farming method yielded twice as much wheat.
examples.cn: 新的耕作方法使小麦产量翻倍。

examples.en: She refused to yield on the question of safety.
examples.cn: 在安全问题上她拒不让步。

examples.en: Drivers must yield to cyclists at the roundabout.
examples.cn: 在环岛处司机必须给骑行者让行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一有得」——田里一有得，就是出产、有收成。

sensesIntro.en: One Germanic verb of handing over runs through farm, road and bank.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示「交出」的日耳曼动词，贯穿田间、马路与银行。

core.en: to give over what one has
core.cn: 把自己有的东西交出去

branches.en: HARVEST LINE: the land gives its crop and the amount is counted.
branches.cn: 收成线：土地交出作物，数量被计量。

branches.en: PRESSURE LINE: resistance stops and control is handed over.
branches.cn: 压力线：抵抗停止，主动权交出。

branches.en: ROAD LINE: one driver lets another go first.
branches.cn: 道路线：一位司机让别人先行。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: capital produces a return.
branches.cn: 资金线：资本产生回报。

branches.en: WEIGHT LINE: a solid thing bends under a load.
branches.cn: 重量线：坚固之物在重压下弯曲。

intro.en: yield is a native Germanic word, so its parts are listed as English building blocks rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: yield 是日耳曼语本土词，这里把各部件当作英语构词块列出。

latinIntro.en: No Latin affixes are involved here, so nothing is listed as Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词缀，故不列拉丁条目。

items.example: Yielding describes what gives way easily.
items.exampleCN: yielding 形容容易让开的东西。

items.example: It looks like yield but means a guard.
items.exampleCN: 它形似 yield，但意思是盾。

definition_zh: 地带；区域；时区；（将……）分成区域
definition_en: an area with a particular purpose or feature, or one of the belts into which the earth is divided
core_image: 地图上一条虚线圈起来的一块，圈内规则一样，圈外换了规矩
scene: 机场广播提醒旅客，过了安检口就进入限制区域。Cars are not allowed in the school zone during the morning hours.
sceneCN: 这里 zone 是「区域」（第 1 个义项：为特定目的划出的一片地方）；句意为上午时段校区内不许车辆通行。地图上虚线围起的一块，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 zone 加 -ing 构成，义为「区划；区域规划」
由 zone 加 -ed 构成，义为「被划成区的」

senses.title: The marked area
senses.definition: an area with a particular purpose or feature, marked off from what is around it
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的或具有特定特征而划出的一片地方
senses.example: Cars are not allowed in the school zone during the morning hours.
senses.exampleCN: 上午时段校区内不许车辆通行。
senses.why: The word came from a Greek noun for a belt or girdle, and a belt around an area is the image behind every later use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自希腊语中表示「腰带」的名词，围住一片地方的带子就是后来各种用法的画面。

senses.title: The bands of the earth
senses.definition: one of the belts into which the earth is divided by climate, by time, or by latitude
senses.definitionCN: 按气候、时间或纬度把地球划成的带
senses.example: The earth is divided into twenty-four time zones.
senses.exampleCN: 地球被划分为二十四个时区。
senses.why: The oldest use fitted the earth itself, where a wide belt of the globe could be marked off and named.
senses.whyCN: 最早的用法直接用在球体上，把地球上一圈宽带划出来命名。

senses.title: The area set aside
senses.definition: an area set aside by law or rule for one use, such as parking, building, or trade
senses.definitionCN: 依法或依规留给某种用途的地片，如停车、建筑或贸易
senses.example: The old harbour became a free trade zone last year.
senses.exampleCN: 旧港区去年成了自由贸易区。
senses.why: A marked strip of land can be reserved by rules, so the belt becomes an official zone with its own regulations.
senses.whyCN: 划出的一条地可以按规则保留，于是这条带子成了有自己的规章的正式区域。

senses.title: To divide into zones
senses.definition: to divide an area into zones, usually for building rules or planning
senses.definitionCN: 把一片地方划成若干区，多用于建筑规则或规划
senses.example: The council zoned the land for housing twenty years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 议会在二十年前就把这片地划作住宅区。
senses.why: The noun turns into an act of drawing the belts on the map, so the same word works as a verb.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了在地图上画带子的动作，于是同一个词也能作动词。

senses.title: The space of focus
senses.definition: a state of deep attention, used in phrases such as in the zone, and in zone out for losing attention
senses.definitionCN: 高度集中的状态，见于 in the zone，以及 zone out 表示走神
senses.example: After ten minutes she was in the zone and finished the paper quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 十分钟后她进入了专注状态，很快就写完了卷子。
senses.why: A zone that encloses an area also encloses a mind, so the word stretches from ground to attention.
senses.whyCN: 围住一片地方的区也能围住一个人的心思，于是这个词从地面伸到注意力。

intro.en: Zone comes from Latin zona and Greek zōnē, which both meant a belt worn round the body.
intro.cn: zone 出自拉丁语 zona 与希腊语 zōnē，两者都指缠在身上的腰带。

items.en: zōnē was the word for a belt or girdle, from a verb meaning to gird up.
items.cn: 希腊语 zōnē 指腰带、束带，出自意为「束起」的动词。

items.en: Latin zona kept the meaning of a belt and was also used for a band of the heavens.
items.cn: 拉丁语 zona 保留腰带之义，也用来指天上的一条带。

items.en: Writers used zonae for the belts of climate that circle the earth.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语作者用 zonae 指环抱地球的气候带。

items.en: The word entered English through French, where it meant both a band and a strip of land.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，法语中既指带子也指一条地。

items.en: English applied zone to areas of special rule, then to time zones and to states of mind.
items.cn: 英语把 zone 用到有特殊规则的区域，后用于时区与心理状态。

note.en: Zone is compared with its family and with other words for marked areas.
note.cn: zone 与自己的词族以及其它表示划定区域的词作对照。

entries.definition: the dividing of land into zones
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生词，区划，区域规划

entries.definition: divided into zones
the quality of a sound, unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，音调，词源不同

entries.definition: a part of a place with no fixed border
entries.definitionCN: 近义，一片区域，边界不固定

entries.definition: a large part of a country or the world
a long band of land or climate
entries.definitionCN: 近义，成带的地域，也与词源相关

normalIntro.en: The image of a belt wrapped round the earth explains most of the word's senses.
normalIntro.cn: 一条缠在地球上的带子，解释了这个词的大多数义项。

normal.en: Time zones are belts wrapped round the globe, each one an hour apart.
normal.cn: 时区就是缠在地球上的带子，每条相隔一小时。

normal.en: Zoning is the act of drawing those belts on the map for planning.
normal.cn: zoning 就是在图上为规划画出这些带子。

normal.en: Greek zōnē meant a girdle, and the verb zōnnynai meant to gird up a garment.
normal.cn: 希腊语 zōnē 意为束带，动词 zōnnynai 意为束起衣服。

normal.en: The verb and the noun share a spelling, so land can be zoned into zones.
normal.cn: 动词与名词拼写相同，所以地可以被划成若干 zone。

normal.en: In the zone means absorbed in the work, while zone out means the opposite.
normal.cn: in the zone 指全神贯注，zone out 则相反。

abstract.en: Picture a waist band tightened around the middle of a body, and then around a whole planet.
abstract.cn: 想象一条腰带先系在腰上，然后系住整个星球。

abstract.en: Picture a dashed line on a car park floor, and everything inside it obeys one rule.
abstract.cn: 想象停车场地上一条虚线，线内一切都守同一条规矩。

abstract.en: Picture a radio dial with bands marked out, each playing something different.
abstract.cn: 想象一个刻着分格的收音机旋钮，每一格放不同的内容。

examples.en: Cars are not allowed in the school zone during the morning hours.
examples.cn: 上午时段校区内不许车辆通行。

examples.en: The earth is divided into twenty-four time zones.
examples.cn: 地球被划分为二十四个时区。

examples.en: The council zoned the land for housing twenty years ago.
examples.cn: 议会在二十年前就把这片地划作住宅区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「宗」——老家按宗族分片而居，一宗一片，界线清清楚楚，这种划出来的一片就是 zone。

root: 经由拉丁语 zona 借自希腊语 zōnē（腰带、束带），词根意为「束起」；后由腰带之义扩展为地球上的气候带与时区。

sensesIntro.en: A belt round the body becomes a belt round the earth, then an area with its own rules, an act of dividing land, and finally a state of attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条系在身上的带子先变成环抱地球的带，再变成有自己规则的区域、划分土地的动作，最后成了注意力的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dashed circle drawn on a map
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上画起的一块虚线圆圈

branches.en: The marked area keeps the picture of a band around something.
branches.cn: 划出的区域保留了「围住某物的一条带」这一画面。

branches.en: The earth's belts give climate and time zones.
branches.cn: 地球上的带子给出气候带与时区。

branches.en: Rules attached to a strip of land turn it into an official zone.
branches.cn: 给一条地附上规则，它就变成正式的区域。

branches.en: Drawing the belts becomes an action, so the noun works as a verb.
branches.cn: 画出这些带子成了动作，于是名词也能作动词。

branches.en: A zone around a mind names deep attention or its loss.
branches.cn: 围着心思的区，指专注或走神。

intro.en: Zone takes -ing and -ed, and appears in compounds such as time zone and school zone.
intro.cn: zone 能加 -ing、-ed，也出现在 time zone、school zone 这类复合词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin zona is a straight borrowing from Greek, and the same root gives English the word girdle through a different path.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 zona 直接借自希腊语，同一词根经另一条路径给出英语的 girdle 一词。

items.exampleCN: 分区规划规则限制建筑高度。

items.example: The land is zoned for farming.

items.meaning: a belt of the earth with one clock time
items.meaningCN: 使用同一钟时的一片地域
items.example: The country spans three time zones.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家跨越三个时区。

items.meaning: an area with speed limits near a school
items.example: Slow down in the school zone.
Greek zōnē is the source of the word.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 zōnē 是这个词的来源。

items.example: Latin zona also names a band of the sky.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 zona 也指天上的一条带。

items.meaning: a belt worn round the waist
items.example: Girdle reached English by another route.
items.exampleCN: girdle 经另一条路径进入英语。
